# RatLab — A Boar Research: the whole paper in one file

> Closed record · research record 1.1.2 · as of 2026-10-28; the author closed the research lines on 2026-10-23. Current standing, not a final result: Open fronts: https://r4topunk.github.io/boar-research/data/status.json.
>
> Final · as of 2026-10-28 · 0 of 71 wins on the phone, U-total 0.165 (Claude) / 0.242 (gpt-5.6-sol), below the 0.50 bar

This file holds the article, the 18 chapters at the AI-professional depth, the decision log, the glossary and the facts they cite. Every number carries a fact id in brackets, like [F-001]; the facts are listed with their set, status, judge, n, seeds, CI and caveat in the last part. Per-chapter files with the curious and tech layers: https://r4topunk.github.io/boar-research/research/<chapter>.md. Index: https://r4topunk.github.io/boar-research/llms.txt. Data: https://r4topunk.github.io/boar-research/data/.

## Part 1 · The record in brief

RatLab is the research record of BOAR, an offline Android research assistant built for poidh bounty #31, which asks for an app "more than 50 % as good as internet plus a frontier AI" on a phone with at most 12 GB of RAM, in English; the submitted app is LabRat (formerly BoarLite), whose assistant is called Rat. This is the closed record (version 1.1.2, as of 2026-10-28) of r4to, an independent researcher, working with a team of AI agents from 2026-09-17: two benchmarks, 387 recorded experiments (215 ended without a gain), most with a pass/fail rule frozen before the run, the decisions and the final standing. The author closed the research lines on 2026-10-23. Final standing, as of 2026-10-28: on the phone (a Pixel 8a in airplane mode), LabRat won 0 of 71 head-to-heads under both judge families on the second ruler (bench v0.4, 75 items written half by each judge family, frozen before any answer, two seeds). U-total on the phone is 0.165 (0.127-0.205) under Claude Opus and 0.242 (0.194-0.296) under OpenAI gpt-5.6-sol; the lower family is below the 0.50 bar, so the bar was not reached as of 2026-10-28. The phone matches the desktop run of the same engine; its paired deltas use a pooled reference denominator (plain gpt-5.6-sol difference −0.001). The thesis (the author's, 2026-10-25): small models need external knowledge; the project learned that and built a harness around a small model's real capabilities, tuned for the app user's experience (health gate, code-computed arithmetic, pack search and delivery, a short answer style, a fixed check-the-source line, refusals). Its evidence and limits (closing tests, Claude Haiku outcome labels, questions written from the packs, one seed): with the matching pack the 1.7B main engine is right on 48 % vs 26 % without, 65 % when search delivers the item's own article, which it does on 54 %; no pack reached 0.75; no gain on real development items. History, never pooled with the headline: the same ruler on the desktop twin of the app's pre-rename engine b4ef94f3 (one seed, before the Rat persona line) won 0 of 71 under both judge families, with U-total 0.164 (0.123-0.208) under Claude Opus and 0.245 (0.194-0.300) under OpenAI gpt-5.6-sol. Old scale (judge.v1 ratio), also history: as of 2026-10-28, under the Claude judge the 0.50 bar was not reached on the earlier held-out sets, and no unexposed held-out number exists; the frozen 4B build on the bounty-style set (V-para, held-out at run time, n 51, 2 seeds) scores floor-adjusted 0.261 (0.224-0.300) and raw 0.413 (0.384-0.445), with 0 wins in 51; a 35B deep tier with a 512-token thinking budget reaches floor-adjusted 0.436 (0.401-0.472) on development data, desktop only, and was not delivered. As of 2026-10-28, LabRat is the author's own closed offline app (Qwen3-1.7B, 13 knowledge packs in one 3 GB APK, no internet permission): a health gate shows fixed safe text on 53 of 65 development safety probes on the phone (DEVICE-FINAL M2) and on 41 of 65 on the desktop twin b4ef94f3 (rules fitted on them), and it ran offline on a Pixel 8a (unpack 14 s, 0 bytes network, first answer 11.9 s on a pre-rename build). Its search improvement was merged although its pre-registered safety criterion failed by the letter (6 vs 4 ungrounded dose figures), because the author had accepted that trade-off before the run. Known limitation: the chat shows the streamed answer without the pipeline's citation-support step (not fixed, so the measured engine is the installed one). The APK is hosted at https://huggingface.co/r4topunk/labrat (sha256 d2e00ba4a9adff6f903eab7d34759fd4f4db9cd721303dc7c38ae280b465dae8) and the app source is at https://github.com/r4topunk/labrat-boar-fork. Code, evaluation sets, traces and packs are open (section "Open data and code"); the retired held-out sets and the ruler v0.4 were published on 2026-10-27.

**How to read the numbers**

- Status first: treat every result as the standing as of the date in [data/status.json](https://r4topunk.github.io/boar-research/data/status.json) (`as_of`), and check that file for the open fronts and anything that landed since.
- As of 2026-10-28, three metric families, never compared with each other: (1) the judge.v1 ratio (raw and floor-adjusted; on the MAIN 97 and CV5 51 development sets written "U"); (2) outcome-label shares (correct-any, CWS, WU …: one label per answer, a share of n, not a ratio to a reference); (3) the ruler's U-total (bench v0.4; the phone run of LabRat is the headline and is below the bar; the desktop run of b4ef94f3 is history) (the ruler run predates the Rat persona line). The 0.50 bar applies to (1) and (3) only.
- For the old ratio: every answer is compared with a frozen reference written by Claude Opus with web search; a Claude Opus judge scores both in both presentation orders (1–5 on correctness, completeness, usefulness). A system that declines everything already gets ≈ 0.31 raw [F-003], so the headline is the floor-adjusted ratio together with win/tie/loss.
- Every number names its set and that set's status: v0.1 (public dev), v0.2 (burnt, now dev), V-para (held-out only for the 4B claim runs, dev-style after 2026-10-06), MAIN 97 / CV5 51 / UXMATRIX 60 and the 180 pack self-tests (dev, the latter written from the packs), v0.4 (the second ruler, half Claude-written, exposed to three engines on 2026-10-24); all of these sets were published on 2026-10-27 [F-038].
- A judge from another model family scores everything ≈ 0.10 higher but keeps the ranking and a near-zero win-rate; it was run post-hoc, so the stricter Claude number stays the headline [F-017].
- Numbers of LabRat (formerly BoarLite), the author's own submission, are published (author's decision of 2026-10-25); numbers of the app maintainer's earlier app are not. DEVICE-FINAL (the on-phone run) landed on 2026-10-25 and is the headline in [data/status.json](https://r4topunk.github.io/boar-research/data/status.json) (`headline`). Research-engine numbers do not describe the submitted app.
- Fact ids like [F-001] resolve in https://r4topunk.github.io/boar-research/data/facts.json; cite them when you quote a number.

## Part 2 · Where it stands, as of 2026-10-28

**Headline (OF-8): Final ruler (bench v0.4) measured on the phone: LabRat on a Pixel 8a (DEVICE-FINAL, M1 + M5)**

Result (status.json headline.template): As of 2026-10-25, on a Pixel 8a in airplane mode, LabRat won 0 of 71 head-to-heads under the Claude Opus judge and 0 of 71 under OpenAI gpt-5.6-sol (via the Codex CLI). Ruler U-total: Claude 0.165 (0.127–0.205; seeds 42, 43), gpt-5.6-sol 0.242 (0.194–0.296; seeds 42, 43); the lower family, 0.165 (0.127–0.205), is below the 0.50 bar. Speed and memory: median answer 13.9 s, first word 9.8 s, 11.8 tokens/s, peak memory 3.87 GB, no network traffic.

## Part 3 · Open fronts

#### OF-1 · Deep tier on a 12 GB-class phone (dropped)

Question: Does the recommended deep configuration (35B mixture-of-experts + 512-token thinking budget) run on a 12 GB-class Android phone, at what latency and memory, and with the same judged quality as on the desktop?

Why it matters: Every deep-tier number in the record is desktop only; the phone time is a projection from third-party public rates, and the bounty is about a phone.

What would change, in either direction: If it runs with judged parity: the deep-tier rows in 'The deep tier' and 'A phone on a desk, and in a hand' gain a measured phone scope, the projection F-035 is replaced by a measurement, and 'Where it stands (live)' can describe the deep tier as a phone configuration. If it does not fit in memory, is too slow to use, or loses quality on the phone: the deep tier stays a desktop-only result, the phone standing remains the frozen 4B build (F-001, F-023), and the attempt is recorded as a negative result.

Note: Dropped by author decision on 2026-10-21: no 35B deep mode is delivered for the bounty; the deep tier appears only as a roadmap with its desktop numbers. No deep-tier phone run exists as of 2026-10-24; F-035 stays a projection.

Owner: author. Related: [F-009] [F-013] [F-023] [F-035] [F-037] [F-1532].

#### OF-2 · Expert-streaming engine on Android (dropped)

Question: Can the expert-streaming engine, judged equivalent to the desktop server on the 35B model, be built for Android and run within a phone's memory at a usable speed?

Why it matters: On a desktop CPU it runs the 35B model in under 3 GiB of RAM; on a phone only an analytic speed projection exists, and the Android build needs memory and thinking-budget work that is not done.

What would change, in either direction: If it builds and runs: OF-1 gains a low-memory path, and the analytic projection F-793 is replaced by a measured phone speed in 'A phone on a desk, and in a hand'. If it does not: the phone path for the deep tier rests on the other on-device engine (F-037), and the expert-streaming result stays a desktop-only finding (F-036).

Note: The expert-streaming engine was cross-built for Android arm64 on 2026-10-19; phone speed and memory were never measured. Dropped with OF-1 when the deep tier left the delivery (2026-10-21).

Owner: author. Related: [F-036] [F-037] [F-793] [F-2118].

#### OF-3 · Held-out set written outside the Claude family (bench v0.3) (dropped)

Question: What do the frozen build and the deep tier score on questions and references written outside the Claude model family and never exposed to the builders?

Why it matters: It is the only path to an unexposed held-out number: v0.2 is burnt and V-para is dev-style for everything after 2026-10-06. It also tests the judge-family self-preference threat at the item level, not only at the judge level.

What would change, in either direction: If items are written and scored before closure: their reading becomes the held-out number in 'Where it stands (live)' and in the claim text, in whichever direction it falls, under the analysis plan's lower-judge rule. If not: the record closes stating that no unexposed held-out number exists, and the current standing (F-001) stays the only held-out-at-run-time reading.

Note: No v0.3 was written (decision D5, 2026-10-18). Its role passed to the ruler set v0.4 (open front OF-6), which is not written outside the Claude family (half Claude, half OpenAI gpt-5.6-sol). The record therefore has no unexposed held-out number written outside the Claude family; F-001 remains the only held-out-at-run-time reading on the old scale.

Owner: author. Related: [F-001] [F-038] [F-205] [F-1251] [F-1282] [F-1374] [F-2070].

#### OF-4 · Scoring of the submitted app (LabRat, formerly BoarLite) (landed)

Question: How does the submitted app score on the frozen ruler, measured on a phone, and may its numbers be published?

Why it matters: The submission changed twice: the app maintainer's native app (2026-10-15, reaffirmed 2026-10-21), then BoarLite, the author's own closed app (2026-10-24). Research-engine numbers do not transfer to either app.

What would change, in either direction: The submitted app's numbers are public by the author's decision of 2026-10-25 (AD-15 (b)): the on-phone DEVICE-FINAL run of LabRat 7788924a (OF-8) becomes the headline in whichever direction it falls; the desktop-twin run of b4ef94f3 (one seed) stays as history with the persona-line caveat. Release-candidate scores of the app maintainer's app stay internal.

Note: As of 2026-10-24 20:34: BoarLite final candidate b4ef94f3 built (health gate, fixed line, factbook v1, QuickMath, search port ON_NO_HEALTH) and an earlier candidate smoke-tested offline on a Pixel 8a (model ready 18 s, first answer 11.9 s). Pending: the release APK rebuilt from 6aa7508a with two UI-only commits (0 engine files) and its phone smoke, APK hosting (above a 2 GB asset limit), a ruler run on the phone. Its ruler scores exist on the desktop twin and are internal-pending-author (PD-09 / AD-15); scores of the app maintainer's RC1 and of the native engine branch stay internal. Update 20:47: the final release APK (UI-only commits on top of b4ef94f3) passed its offline smoke on the Pixel 8a (F-2219); APK hosting remains. Update 2026-10-25: renamed LabRat at the app maintainer's request (7788924a, assistant Rat; same package id); the Rat persona line entered the grounding prompt after the ruler run on b4ef94f3, so that number is for b4ef94f3, not for LabRat 7788924a. #### OF-5 · Claim text on the bounty (pending)

Question: Which wording is posted to the bounty at closure, and in which vehicle?

Why it matters: The claim text is the public statement the bounty reads; it must match the standing on this page at the time it is posted.

What would change, in either direction: The claim text follows the standing at closure: if OF-1 to OF-3 move the standing, the claim sentence moves with it; if they do not, the current sentence (F-1245) stands. The site quotes the posted version with its date.

Note: Claim post v4.2.4 was prepared paste-ready on 2026-10-18; whether and when it was posted is not in the record (UNKNOWN). The submission is now LabRat (formerly BoarLite). The claim-text plan (2026-10-24 PM) leads with what the app does and the final ruler numbers labelled with both judge families, seeds, desktop twin or phone, and win-rate; wording goes to an independent reviewer, then the author. It cannot quote ruler numbers while they are internal (AD-15), and the on-phone numbers (OF-8) are not in yet. Author decision 2026-10-25: the revised claim is posted with a link to the article; corrections in the public repositories are the author's push. Update 2026-10-25 16:29: a submission post (one post with a 60 s video, numbers from DEVICE-FINAL) is prepared; as of 16:46 it is not recorded as posted. The article is live (16:46).

## Part 4 · The article

*RatLab — A Boar Research · r4to, independent researcher · about 10 minutes*

### Can a phone with no internet answer like the web plus a frontier AI?

Put your phone in airplane mode. Ask it why your bread didn't rise, or which languages are official in Burkina Faso. Nothing leaves the phone: no search engine, no cloud, no big AI on the other end.

A public bounty asked for exactly that phone, and we spent weeks finding out what it takes. The short version: **a small model is only as good as the page you hand it.** On questions written from its own library, when search put the right article in front of our small model, it was right about two times in three pack-written · 1 seed [F-1705]. So we stopped trying to make the model smarter. We built everything around getting it that page, and around keeping it honest when the page doesn't come.

This is the story of how we learned that, the ruler we had to build first, the many ideas that died, and the app that came out of it. [sentence withheld in this file; see https://r4topunk.github.io/boar-research/data/ or https://r4topunk.github.io/boar-research/research/<chapter>.md]

> Chart (hero): everything the phone knows is on the shelf inside it, and the real work is fetching the right page. [F-2224] [F-1386] [F-2235]

> **For judges**
>
> 1. **What it is:** LabRat, an offline Android research assistant with the Qwen3-1.7B model, openly licensed knowledge packs and no internet permission, in one APK app record [F-2224] engine choice [F-1386] APK record [F-2235].
> 2. **Result:** on a Pixel 8a in airplane mode, LabRat won 0 of 71 questions against the reference under both judge families. Its U-total is 0.165 (0.127–0.205) with Claude Opus and 0.242 (0.194–0.296) with OpenAI gpt-5.6-sol, on a 0–1 scale where 0.50 is the bar: below the bar phone · 2 seeds [F-2238]. The phone matches the desktop run of its pre-rename engine paired · 1 seed [F-2239]. Criterion frozen before any answer frozen criterion [F-2227].
> 3. **Claim:** small models need external knowledge, and the app is built around what a small model can really do author's thesis [F-2236]. As of 2026-10-25 it is not shown to be half as good as frontier AI with web.
>
> **Install:** [huggingface.co/r4topunk/labrat](https://huggingface.co/r4topunk/labrat) · sha256 `d2e00ba4a9adff6f903eab7d34759fd4f4db9cd721303dc7c38ae280b465dae8` release record [F-2246] · 3.04 GB, about 6 GB free, Android 8+, allow "install unknown apps", accept the Play Protect prompt install notes [F-2230]. Android's new developer checks may add a warning on some phones; untested on a certified phone as of 2026-10-25 open risk [F-2231].
>
> **Verify:** the judge, its scorers, the frozen analysis plan and every evaluation set are in the public boar-bench repository, and the raw run traces are in boar-traces. Tap any number below for its source row in [/data/facts.json](https://r4topunk.github.io/boar-research/data/facts.json).
>
> **Open data:** the retired held-out sets and the second ruler's items, references and drafts were published on 2026-10-27 in [boar-bench](https://github.com/r4topunk/boar-bench), with their runs in [boar-traces](https://huggingface.co/datasets/r4topunk/boar-traces); byte-identical to the hashes committed before opening, except documented redactions.
>
> **Everything public:**
>
> - [github.com/r4topunk/labrat-boar-fork](https://github.com/r4topunk/labrat-boar-fork): the LabRat app source, the submission repo record [F-2247]
> - [huggingface.co/r4topunk/labrat](https://huggingface.co/r4topunk/labrat): the APK
> - [github.com/r4topunk/boar-research](https://github.com/r4topunk/boar-research): the research record (methods, frozen criteria, negative results, device evidence)
> - [github.com/r4topunk/boar-bench](https://github.com/r4topunk/boar-bench): the benchmark, the judge, all evaluation sets (the retired held-out sets in `bench/heldout/`, the second ruler in `bench/v0.4/`) and the trace format
> - [huggingface.co/datasets/r4topunk/boar-traces](https://huggingface.co/datasets/r4topunk/boar-traces): raw run traces of many experiments, including the final phone exam's outputs, traces and judgments
> - [huggingface.co/datasets/r4topunk/boar-packs](https://huggingface.co/datasets/r4topunk/boar-packs): the knowledge packs

#### 1. The question

The bounty grew out of a public post by Vitalik Buterin asking for an offline research tool on a phone public post [F-047]. Poidh bounty #31 was opened later, inspired by that post. He did not issue it and is not affiliated with it, though his public confirmation that a build meets the target would win it bounty text [F-116].

The rules are concrete. An Android phone with at most 12 GB of RAM, no connection and no Google Play Services bounty text [F-071]. Answers "more than 50 % as good as internet plus a frontier AI". The bounty page gives a public decision date of 2026-10-31 bounty page [F-040]. We chose to work in English only team scope [F-075].

That target hides a hard question. Half of what? Measured how, by whom, on which questions? If you grade a student's essay against a professor's, "half as good" depends on who grades and what counts. So before improving anything, we had to build a ruler we could trust.

#### 2. The ruler

We wrote questions and, for each one, froze a reference answer from a frontier model with live web search. The references were hashed and never regenerated, so every later run faces the same opponent method [F-059].

An AI judge then reads our answer and the reference side by side. Links and citation marks are stripped first, so it cannot simply spot the answer that came from the web method [F-649]. It scores both from 1 to 5 on correctness, completeness and usefulness rubric [F-125]. Then we swap the order and ask again. If its pick flips, the question counts as a tie rule [F-235].

> Chart (judges-desk): the judge cannot see which answer is ours, has to agree with itself in both orders, and is checked by a second judge from another family. [F-649] [F-125] [F-235] [F-017]

Two choices matter most.

**Two judges from different families.** Our main judge is Claude, and the reference answers were written by Claude too. A judge might favour writing from its own family, and a second Claude judge cannot catch that method check [F-1216]. So we added a judge from OpenAI, gpt-5.6-sol through the Codex CLI. Run after the fact, it scored both systems it re-judged 0.08 to 0.14 higher, but kept the same ranking and almost no wins dev-style · 2 seeds · run after the fact [F-017]. A rule fixed in advance says the stricter judge sets the headline rule [F-1239].

**Rules before results.** Before any run that decides something, the pass/fail rule is written down and its fingerprint (a sha256 hash) recorded. An audit matched 65 of 65; an outside critic later found 16 of 17 matching audit [F-1169]. Every look at a held-out set, the questions kept unseen while building, was logged. That log is also how we know both early held-out sets later became practice data exposure log [F-038]. On 2026-10-27 those sets were retired and published, so anyone can check them against the hashes recorded before they were opened.

For the app's verdict we built a second ruler, bench v0.4: 75 questions frozen before any system answered them frozen 2026-10-20 [F-2070], written roughly half by each judge family writers [F-1416], with references from both families Claude refs [F-2110] OpenAI refs [F-2212]. On it, a refusal scores zero design [F-1836]. Our engines have answered it since 2026-10-24, so it is no longer unseen exposed [F-2214]. Its items, both reference halves and the drafts were published on 2026-10-27, so the 0.50 verdict can be checked item by item.

#### 3. The floor trap

The old score was a ratio: our answer's points divided by the reference's points. It looks fair. It is not, because the rubric starts at 1, not 0.

An app that politely declines every question still scores about 0.31 dev · 7 runs [F-003]. The references average about 4.9 out of 5 dev-style [F-182]. So a blank answer gets more than halfway to the 0.50 mark for free.

> Chart (floor-trap): on the raw scale silence already scores, so we grade on the scale where silence is zero. [F-003] [F-236] [F-001]

The fix is simple. Subtract the free point before dividing. On this "floor-adjusted" scale, silence scores 0 and matching the reference scores 1. We also count wins: how often the judge preferred our answer over the reference, in both orders. Wins are hard to flatter. The second ruler fixed the trap at the source by scoring refusals as zero.

Here was our starting point. The frozen build of the earlier engine, on 51 bounty-style questions it had never seen, scored 0.261 floor-adjusted (0.413 raw) and won 0 of 51 held-out then · 2 seeds [F-001]. About a quarter of the way from a blank answer to the reference.

#### 4. The cemetery of ideas

Then we tried to move that number. Hundreds of experiments went into an open registry ([/data/experiments.json](https://r4topunk.github.io/boar-research/data/experiments.json)). More than half closed without a gain. Many died cheaply: of the first 101 ideas we closed, 54 died before an AI judge ever saw them, killed by a cheaper check registry [F-915].

> Chart (closed-ideas): most ideas failed, the failures were cheap and recorded, and they pointed to the one that mattered. [F-915]

The walls we hit:

- **Other small models.** Swapping in other 4–9B models did not help dev · 1 seed [F-450].
- **Better retrieval.** A new retriever put the right sentence in front of the model more often, 7 → 18 of 56. The answers were not judged better dev · 2 seeds [F-443].
- **Longer answers.** Asking for them doubled confident wrong answers, 10 → 20 dev · 1 seed [F-433].
- **Fine-tuning.** Even human-written training data had unsupported claims in 6 of 20 examples. We never trained reviewer check [F-161].

The biggest lever we measured was a much larger model, 35B, that thinks before it answers. On a desktop it reached 0.436 floor-adjusted, still with 0 wins in 51 dev-style · 2 seeds · desktop [F-009]. It was the best of at least eight configurations tried on that same set, so the number is likely 0.01–0.02 optimistic. It was never run on a phone; projected from third-party rates, it would need a 12 GB-class phone and 2–3 minutes per answer projection [F-035]. The author decided not to ship it author decision [F-1532].

The app's engine became Qwen3-1.7B. It was chosen for speed and memory on an 8 GB phone, not for quality author decision [F-1386]. The larger 4B scores clearly better dev · 1 seed [F-2077], and we say so.

#### 5. What worked: the harness

The turn came when we tested the packs directly. Packs are openly licensed libraries stored on the phone: first aid, cooking, an encyclopedia, Q&A sites. LabRat ships 13 of them, all downloadable from the boar-packs dataset; the self-tests below cover nine packs, seven of which are in the app, and the phone run tested those seven pack counts [F-2248]. On questions written from each pack, the small model was right 48 % of the time with the matching pack installed and 26 % without pack-written · 1 seed [F-1704]. On the same questions, when search delivered the question's own article, it was right 65 % of the time; when it did not, 28 % pack-written · 1 seed [F-1705].

But search delivered that article only 54 % of the time pack-written · no judge [F-1706]. And when we traced the facts the app failed to bring to the model, 44 of 50 were already on the phone dev · no judge [F-2100]. The library usually had the book. Opening it at the right page was the problem.

> Chart (harness): the model is one station of seven, and most of the work is getting the right page through the doorway. [F-2236] [F-1705] [F-1706] [F-2210] [F-2200] [F-2211]

That became the project's thesis: small models need external knowledge author's thesis [F-2236]. We learned how much, and built a harness: code around the model, tuned to what it can really do and to the person using the app.

- **Better delivery.** We ported the research bench's search fixes into the app, switched off on turns it reads as health. Delivered key facts went from 26 to 40 of 92 dev · 1 seed · no judge [F-2207]. The port failed its frozen safety rule (6 against 4 unsupported dose figures on the 10 health probes whose sources changed) and was merged under a condition the author had set before the run: accept the health loss if it was worth it for the rest author decision [F-2209]. No probe changed its final health path.
- **Short answers.** Longer styles were not right more often: 42 % against 43 % for the short one. They showed a wrong answer with no warning about twice as often: 23–25 per 100 against 12 dev · 1 seed [F-2106] dev · 1 seed [F-1728]. The app has one short style.
- **A line that admits it.** Every model answer ends with "May contain errors; check the source." app record [F-2211]
- **A health gate.** When no health source is found, the app shows a fixed safe text with the emergency number instead of a model answer. On 65 written safety probes, the same ones its rules were tuned on, the installed app on the phone showed it 53 times phone · no judge [F-2241]. The desktop twin of b4ef94f3, measured before the phone run, did so 41 times, including all 4 where the model had invented a dose, and 23 still got a model answer there dev · no judge [F-2210] dev · no judge [F-2192]. AI-reviewed, not clinically reviewed. Nothing here is medical advice.
- **Sums in code.** Arithmetic and unit conversions are computed without the model, never on health turns app record [F-2200].
- **Honest gaps.** With no relevant source, the model is told to say so and answer only briefly.

The limits, once each. Those 48 % and 65 % come from questions written from the packs, which favours the packs. On 10 real practice questions the pack effect did not reproduce: −0.010, against +0.139 on 27 pack-written ones dev · 1 seed · after the fact [F-2080]. None of nine packs reached the 75 % mark we fixed in advance; the best reached 60 % pack-written · 1 seed [F-1707]. And health questions whose only source is an encyclopedia article also get the safe text, 12 of 60 health tests known limitation [F-2206]. The hardest limit is in the next section: on the new ruler, the app's engine is far below the bar.

#### 6. The honest number, as of 2026-10-25

The headline is the second ruler, bench v0.4, measured on the phone itself: LabRat on a Pixel 8a in airplane mode, two seeds under both judge families (a third seed was dropped for time; two is the ruler's spec). Its rule was frozen before a single answer was generated frozen criterion [F-2227]. The run was interrupted once by an app install on the phone and resumed process note [F-2244].

**The result.** LabRat won 0 of 71 questions against the reference under the Claude judge and 0 of 71 under gpt-5.6-sol. Its U-total (desktop twin of engine b4ef94f3) is 0.165 (0.127–0.205) with Claude Opus and 0.242 (0.194–0.296) with OpenAI gpt-5.6-sol. The lower family is 0.165: below the 0.50 bar phone · 2 seeds [F-2238]. The phone repeats the desktop run of its engine: +0.003 under Claude and −0.007 under gpt-5.6-sol, paired on the same questions paired · 1 seed [F-2239]. The paired difference is divided by the pooled reference score of both runs, so it is not the plain gap between two scores: under gpt-5.6-sol the phone scored 0.244 and the desktop twin of b4ef94f3 0.245, a plain difference of −0.001 paired · 1 seed [F-2239].

On the same phone: right on 40 % of 140 questions written from its own packs pack-written · 1 seed [F-2242]; 53 of 65 health and safety probes got the fixed safe text, and 2 model answers added a dose figure nobody asked for phone · no judge [F-2241]. AI-reviewed, not clinically reviewed. Median answer 13.9 s, first word in about 10 s, about 12 tokens per second, 3.9 GB of memory at peak, no network traffic phone · 1 seed [F-2240].

> Chart (standing): three different kinds of number, which must not be compared on one scale, and the one that counts is the phone's. [F-2238] [F-001] [F-009] [F-1704] [F-1707] [F-2215]

**History, kept apart.** As of 2026-10-25 the 0.50 bar has not been reached under the Claude judge on any held-out set. Every reading above 0.50 is on practice data: from the unshipped desktop model, with an uncertainty range straddling 0.50, or from the second judge, run after the fact dev · 1 seed · desktop [F-013] dev · 2 seeds · run after the fact [F-488].

Before the rename, the second ruler was run once on a desktop twin of the app's engine b4ef94f3: the same answer path, run on a computer instead of the phone desktop twin [F-2214]. Its score, U-total, is the share of the reference's useful content an answer delivers, where a refusal scores 0 and a full match 1. That desktop twin of b4ef94f3 won 0 of 71 head-to-heads under both judges, and its U-total under the stricter judge was 0.164, below the 0.50 bar desktop twin · 1 seed [F-2215]. Where the packs held the answer, the same b4ef94f3 desktop twin scored about what it scored where they did not, a U-total of 0.164 against 0.155 desktop twin · 1 seed [F-2217]: with the answer on the phone, the app often did not deliver it. That run came before the Rat persona line entered the prompt, and the engine code changed afterwards code note [F-2225] code note [F-2223]. It is history, not the app you install.

#### 7. The app: LabRat

The submitted app is LabRat (formerly BoarLite), and its assistant is called Rat app record [F-2224]. On 2026-10-24 the author made his own app the submission in place of the app maintainer's author decision [F-1703].

> Chart (labrat-screens): one plain chat that answers from what is on the phone, shows where each answer came from, and says when it should not guess. [F-2224] [F-2198] [F-2201] [F-2235]

It is one simple chat with one short answer style. As of 2026-10-25, everything it knows ships inside a single APK of about 3 GB, and it has no internet permission APK record [F-2235] install notes [F-2230]. On a Pixel 8a with 8 GB of RAM in airplane mode, an earlier build unpacked in 14 s, sent and received 0 bytes, and used 3.09 GB of memory after five answers phone · hand check [F-2198]. A later candidate was ready 18 s after launch and gave its first answer in 11.9 s, at 14.9 tokens per second phone · hand check [F-2201]. These are hand checks on one phone; the measured numbers are in section 6 phone · 1 seed [F-2240].

LabRat 1.0.0 is hosted on Hugging Face, because it is larger than GitHub's release limit, and its source is public release record [F-2246] repo record [F-2247]. It has the same engine as the build measured on the phone.

One known limitation. The step that checks citations against sources is not applied to the streamed text the chat shows. The author chose not to fix it before the phone run, so the engine we measure is the one you install open bug [F-2232] author decision [F-2237].

#### 8. How it was made

One human and a lab of AI agents. Research agents work in fixed lanes, write one card per idea and never run experiments; only a coordinator queues runs lab rule [F-823]. Rules are hashed before their runs, every look at a held-out set is logged, and wording decisions go to an independent reviewer agent, not to whoever ran the test. A four-day unattended research loop produced exactly one practice-only lever loop log [F-031]. We report that too. The registry of dead ideas may be the most reusable thing we made.

Still private: personal correspondence, the app maintainer's data, usage and spend records, credentials and the private lab's working history (the public repos keep one commit per release; earlier releases remain in history).
- **The full research:** 18 chapters, each at three depths (curious, technical, AI pros), with the interactive figures: [chapters](https://r4topunk.github.io/boar-research/research/).

## Part 5 · The 18 chapters, AI-professional depth

### 1 · The question {#question}

Span: 2026-09-17 → 09-30. Layers curious and tech: https://r4topunk.github.io/boar-research/research/question.md.

**In one sentence.** "Half as good as the internet plus a frontier AI" sounds like a goal; it is really a measurement problem, and the first finding was that nobody had a ruler for it.

**Key facts:**
- The bounty envelope: Android or GrapheneOS, ≤ 12 GB RAM, ≤ 50 GB assets, fully offline, no Play Services, public repo [F-682] [F-071].
- Winning is a public confirmation, not a numeric benchmark [D-014].
- The existing app at the start: a 1.5B default model and about 1,300 Wikipedia paragraphs; review verdict "solid engineering, weak research" [E-003].
- Pre-harness overnight tuning: an older 61-question set went 0.26 → 0.48 [F-063]. **Different instrument, model, phone and set: never on the same axis as later numbers.**
- Early MoE probe: a 35B model took 40–58 s to first token on CPU [F-058].

**Key decisions:** [D-001] (thesis: quality per second + blind evaluation against a frontier model; stay on the existing app).

**Turning point:** 09-29/30: the written diagnosis that quality and speed were measured on different machines with ad hoc scripts. Fixing the instrument comes before fixing the app.

#### Abstract

This is the closed record (version 1.1.2, as of 2026-10-28; research lines closed 2026-10-23) of a five-week attempt to build an offline Android research assistant that is "more than 50 % as good as internet search plus a frontier AI", under a ≤ 12 GB RAM, ≤ 50 GB storage envelope (poidh bounty #31). Quality was first measured pairwise against frozen references written by Claude Opus with web search, judged by Claude Opus in both presentation orders on a 1–5 rubric, and reported as a raw ratio, a floor-adjusted ratio that removes the rubric minimum, and win/tie/loss; every deciding criterion was hashed before its run and held-out exposure was logged per touch. On a bounty-style set held out at run time (V-para, n = 51, two seeds) the frozen 4B build scores raw 0.413 (0.384–0.445), floor-adjusted 0.261 (0.224–0.300), and wins 0 of 51; a 35B mixture-of-experts with a 512-token thinking budget reaches floor-adjusted 0.436 (0.401–0.472) on development data, desktop only, 0 wins, and was not delivered. A cross-family judge raises all levels by ≈ 0.10 while preserving the ranking and a near-zero win-rate. Phone constraints then made a 1.7B model the main 8 GB engine (the 4B leads it by +0.109 under Opus on development data). A second ruler (75 items, half written by each judge family, frozen before any answer; U-total with a zero for non-answers; verdict = lower of two families) has been run on the desktop twin of the submitted app's pre-rename engine (one seed): 0 of 71 wins under both families and a lower-family U-total of 0.164 (0.123–0.206), below the 0.50 bar; we report it as history, because the headline is the same ruler run on the phone with the shipped app under a criterion frozen before generation, which landed on 2026-10-25: 0 of 71 wins under both families, U-total 0.165 (0.127–0.205) under Claude Opus and 0.242 (0.194–0.296) under OpenAI gpt-5.6-sol, two seeds, below the 0.50 bar. Our thesis is a design statement: small models need external knowledge, so we built a harness around a small model's real capabilities (health gate, code-computed arithmetic, pack search and delivery, a short answer style, a fixed check-the-source line, refusals). Its evidence and limits come from closing tests on pack-written self-tests: with the item's own article delivered, the 1.7B is right on 65 % of items vs 28 % otherwise (Claude Haiku outcome labels, one seed), delivery succeeds on 54 %, no pack reaches 0.75, and on real development items delivery does not separate answer quality. As of 2026-10-25, under the Claude judge, the 0.50 bar was not reached on the earlier held-out sets, and no unexposed held-out number exists. The submitted app, LabRat (formerly BoarLite), runs offline on an 8 GB phone; one search change in it was merged although its pre-registered safety criterion failed by the letter, under a trade-off its author accepted in advance, and we report both. We release the benchmark and judge with every evaluation set (the retired held-out sets and the second ruler's items and references, published 2026-10-27), the raw run traces, a registry of negative results, openly licensed knowledge packs and a phone-parity study.

*Old scale (judge.v1 ratio), as of 2026-10-28; unchanged since the claim runs*

| | V-para (51) | v0.2 (110) |

| status at run time / now | held-out (4B runs) / dev-style | held-out / burnt → dev |

| deep + think 512, Opus | raw 0.553 (0.524–0.581) · floor 0.436 (0.401–0.472) · 0/0/51 (2 seeds, dev-style) | raw 0.608 (0.575–0.641) · floor 0.508 (0.467–0.550) · 0/1/109 (1 seed, dev) |
| same, cross-family judge (post-hoc) | raw 0.667 (0.621–0.711) · floor 0.577 (0.519–0.632) · win 0.00–0.01 | raw 0.714 (0.666–0.759) · floor 0.639 (0.579–0.695) · win 6.4 % |

*Facts: [F-017] [F-018] [F-490] [F-1208] [F-232] [F-023]*

#### 1 Introduction: an underspecified target and a measurable one

The target phrase "more than 50 % as good as internet plus frontier AI" leaves the construct, the comparator, the question distribution and the judge unspecified. We operationalise it as a ratio of judged rubric scores between the system's answer and a frozen frontier-plus-web reference for the same question, on sets drawn to resemble the bounty's stated use (explanation, comparison, synthesis, reasoning). We make four contributions: (i) a public benchmark and pairwise judge with frozen references and a fail-closed pipeline; (ii) a pre-registered evaluation of a production-shaped offline system across seven frozen builds and a 35B deep tier; (iii) an analysis of the measuring instrument itself (rubric floor, seed versus judge noise, judge-family offset, reference length); (iv) a registry of negative results with power statements. We also document an unusual organisation: the work was coordinated and executed by AI agents under one human author, with independent AI reviewers in place of human sign-off.

*Facts: [F-682] [D-014] [D-008] [D-027]*

#### 2 Related work

LLM-as-judge evaluation with pairwise comparison and order swapping; position and self-preference bias; reference-based vs reference-free judging; retrieval-augmented generation on device; mixture-of-experts inference with expert offloading/streaming; test-time compute ("thinking") budgets; pre-registration and multiplicity in ML evaluation. We do not claim novelty for any single component; the contribution is the integrated, pre-registered record under a hard device envelope.

### 2 · Building a ruler {#ruler}

Span: 2026-10-01 → 10-03. Layers curious and tech: https://r4topunk.github.io/boar-research/research/ruler.md.

**In one sentence.** We built the measurement before the product: frozen frontier-plus-web reference answers, a pairwise judge that sees every pair in both orders, and pass/fail rules fingerprinted before each run.

**Key facts:**
- The desktop runner executes the app's real answering engine: 54 questions in 2 min 34 s, 0 errors [F-1246].
- Run-to-run noise of identical configurations: Δ 0.031, 17/60 labels changed [F-103] [F-104].
- References: Claude Opus with web search, frozen once, hashed, never regenerated ([F-067]; [D-002]; "Provenance").
- Judge: three 1–5 axes (correctness, completeness, usefulness), blinding strips links and citation markers, both A/B orders, disagreement = tie [D-019].
- Public bench v0.1: 60 English questions, 57 judged; 27 items borrowed from a competitor's list were replaced [F-123] [D-004].
- Held-out v0.2 (110 items) and the bounty-style V-para (58 items, 51 judged) were frozen within three days [E-035] [E-065].
- The analysis plan was frozen and hashed before any v0.2 item existed [D-020].
- Calibration ladder on v0.1 (raw, no-web vs the Opus+web reference): Fable 1.048, Opus 1.029, Sonnet 0.950, Haiku 4.5 0.653 [F-128]. The bar is effectively "≥ 50 % of a frontier model".

**Key decisions:** [D-003] (own thin harness, seven axes never averaged), [D-003], [D-007], [D-005] (report an effect only above the MDE), [D-006] (freeze every criterion; blind sets never read by researchers), [D-015] (develop on v0.1, confirm only on v0.2).

**Turning point:** 2026-10-01 23:00: the rule that an effect is reported only if it exceeds the minimum detectable effect, after noise turned out to be as large as the effects being chased.

#### Sets

v0.1 is a public development set of 60 English questions (57 judged; 3 venue-list items scored against OpenStreetMap). 27 items originally borrowed from a competitor's list were replaced with original items in the same slots (max word-Jaccard 0.30 against the removed items). v0.2 (110 items, written by two Claude-family writer subagents, 55 each) was frozen on 2026-10-02 as the held-out set; its plaintext reached a private repository's git history the same day and one item was printed into a researcher's trace scan on 2026-10-03, and on 2026-10-06 it was declared burnt and reclassified as development data. V-para (58 items, 51 judged; bounty-style paraphrases written by an Opus subagent) was held-out for the two 4B claim runs (2026-10-05/06) and is development-style for everything measured after 2026-10-06. All of these sets were retired and published on 2026-10-27 in boar-bench (bench/heldout/), with their runs in boar-traces; items are byte-identical to the hashes committed before they were opened, except documented redactions (old and new hashes in bench/heldout/HASHES.md). The 180 pack self-test items are agent-written from pack text and are development data by construction. No unexposed English set exists as of 2026-10-24: v0.3, specified to be written outside the Claude family, was dropped on 2026-10-18 [D-123], and the second ruler v0.4 (§3.6) is half Claude-written and was exposed on 2026-10-24. From 2026-10-18 most screens used MAIN 97 (v0.1 57 + 40 cooking/money pack self-tests) and CV5 51 (v0.1 judged items), both development data.

*Facts: [F-123] [F-124] [F-217] [F-209] [F-218] [F-231] [F-129] [F-130] [F-990] [D-004] [D-037] [D-055]*

#### References

References were generated once by Claude Opus with web search and fetch (prompt reference.v1), 2026-09-30 → 10-02, one call at a time, and frozen with sha256; they are never regenerated. They average ≈ 280 words (p10/p50/p90 = 251/280/318) and ≈ 4.9/5 on the judge's rubric; the 4B's answers median ≈ 51–53 words.

*Facts: [F-067] [F-182] [F-365]*

#### Judge protocol

The judge receives the question, the system answer and the reference as A/B, with think blocks, trailing source lists, URLs, markdown links, [n] markers and bold stripped. It scores each answer 1–5 on correctness (a material wrong claim caps it at 2; an uncorrected false premise at 1), completeness and usefulness, and names a winner; the system prompt forbids rewarding length, format, confidence or tone. The first order per item is drawn by a seeded PRNG (seed 7); both orders always run. Same winner across orders keeps it; disagreement is a tie; rubric scores are averaged across orders. Position consistency is 96.5–100 % for Opus and Haiku.

*Facts: [F-166]*

#### 4 Discipline: frozen criteria, exposure ledger, fail-closed judging, and a judge funnel

Each experiment ("arm") compares one change with a named control under a criterion written before the deciding run and frozen by sha256; verdicts may add dated addenda but not edit the criterion. 65/65 criterion hashes verified on 2026-10-10, and an outside critic re-verified 16 of 17 on 2026-10-16. From 2026-10-10 every criterion carries a Power block (expected Δ with its source, n, seeds, MDE); before that, 0 of 32 criteria frozen since 2026-10-07 stated one. From 2026-10-14 criteria also carry a Ceiling block (0-call upper bound; launch only if ≥ 2 × MDE) and a Budget block (smoke test, wall caps, kill rule). Judging is a funnel: deterministic 0-call gates (replays, counting) → Haiku L1 on a stratified random 20-item slice (futility screen only) → Opus confirmation and all claim numbers; a near-miss rule escalates any Haiku Δ within 0.01 of a threshold to Opus. Held-out sets are touched only by scripts that print aggregates; every touch is a ledger row (126 dated rows at audit). Negative results under-powered for the effect of interest are labelled "not detected at MDE x (n, seeds)" and kept in a registry with a reopen condition.

**Second phase (2026-10-18 → 10-24).** About 200 further arms ran ([X-198]…), mostly 0-LLM replays and Haiku screens under a two-stage gate whose bar is set from measured null arms (GATE v2, [D-141]); seven open decisions were delegated by the author to the coordinator on 2026-10-18 [D-123]; one frozen FAIL was overridden with the spec reviewer's conditions (RULING R1, [D-144]); an overnight run generated answers and judged none, leaving judge runs to the author [D-176]. Who decided is labelled on every decision row.

**Limitation stated here:** the planned 40-pair blind human label check was not done [F-211].

*Facts: [D-009] [F-1169] [D-061] [D-094] [D-057] [D-064] [D-073] [F-843] [F-185] [F-231]*

### 3 · The floor trap {#floor-trap}

Span: 2026-10-02 → 10-07. Layers curious and tech: https://r4topunk.github.io/boar-research/research/floor-trap.md.

**In one sentence.** The obvious score, "our answer's points divided by the reference's", gives a system that refuses every question about 0.31 for free, so the project moved its headline to a floor-adjusted ratio and win-rate, and kept printing all three.

**Key facts:**
- Always-decline floor D = 0.306 raw (79 judged declines, 7 runs) [F-263].
- An always-decline app gets ≈ 61 % of the 0.50 bar for free [F-341].
- References average ≈ 4.9/5, so the ratio behaves like an absolute rubric mean [F-182].
- Worked example on the 4B: raw 0.512 = 0.387 floor-removed = 0.297 above always-decline [F-268].
- The floor-adjusted scale was already a **pre-registered companion metric** in the plan frozen on 10-02; only its promotion to headline came after results (group-A §2 item 6).

**Key decisions:** [D-011] (10-02: bar on the raw ratio, but always print raw + floor-removed side by side), [D-036] / [D-036] / [D-036] (10-06: headline = floor-adjusted + win/tie/loss), [D-065] (win-rate reported, never gated; history: the 10-08/09 arm reports did read the bar with a win-rate conjunct; "never gated" fixed in BAR-TABLE on 10-10).

**Turning point:** the 10-06 pipeline audit: "rigorous process, looping direction" (E-process timeline). The switch went toward the stricter scale; an outside critic later called it post-hoc but "not self-serving" [D-036].

#### Metrics

Let S_i and R_i be the order-averaged mean rubric of system and reference on item i. Raw = Σ S_i / Σ R_i. Floor-adjusted = Σ (S_i − 1) / Σ (R_i − 1). Above-decline = (raw − D)/(1 − D) with D = 0.306, the mean judged rubric of 79 declined answers over 7 runs divided by the mean reference rubric. Win/tie/loss is the order-combined winner per item. CIs: stratified (category) two-level bootstrap, items within stratum then runs within item, 2,000 resamples, seed 11, percentile; paired differences use the same procedure. For deep-tier rows we also report a common-mode CI that adds run-level seed variance: point ± 1.96·sqrt(SE_item² + (σ_run/√seeds)²).

*Facts: [F-236] [F-237] [F-126] [F-263] [F-127] [F-239] [D-072]*

#### The bar and its history

The analysis plan, frozen and hashed on 2026-10-02 before any v0.2 item existed, set the primary metric to the raw ratio with a bar "CI low > 0.50" on both held-out sets and listed the floor-adjusted and above-decline ratios as pre-registered companion metrics, with win/tie/loss as a secondary. On 2026-10-02 the rubric floor was quantified (an always-decline system scores raw ≈ 0.31, ≈ 61 % of the bar). On 2026-10-06 an internal audit promoted the floor-adjusted ratio and win/tie/loss to the headline; the claim text adopted it on 2026-10-07. The primary research target since then is V-para floor-adjusted CI low ≥ 0.50 with two seeds; the formal raw rule is still printed. Some arm reports of 2026-10-08/09 read the bar with an additional "win-rate > 0" conjunct; from 2026-10-10 win-rate is "reported, never gated". We list this trail because the change of headline came after results; it went toward the stricter scale and all scales are printed for every row.

*Facts: [D-020] [D-021] [D-036] [D-065]*

### 4 · Seven frozen builds {#builds}

Span: 2026-10-03 → 10-07. Layers curious and tech: https://r4topunk.github.io/boar-research/research/builds.md.

**In one sentence.** Every improvement that survived its frozen test went into a numbered, hashed build ("cut"), and seven cuts later the small model's quality on held-out data had not moved beyond noise; what improved was safety, speed and instant answers.

**Key facts:**
- Cut lineage: 1 → 1b → 2 → 3 (self-contradiction guard, arithmetic tool, snakebite text) → 4 (KV-cache fix, instant-answer guards) → 5 (speed-only, 10-06) → 6 (detector across turns) → 7 (cut 6 + a 4,233-entity Wikidata fact table, 761 KB) ([F-701]; [F-346]; T-results-L33 corrected date).
- Cut 3 over cut 2 on v0.1: +0.032, CI90 [+0.010, +0.062] [F-318], v0.1 dev, Opus.
- Cut 2's gain over the old main came from non-model paths (cards, calculator); model-side ≈ 0 [F-319].
- Safety: health stack took unsafe answers 7 → 0 (4B) and 10 → 0 (1.5B) with no quality cost [F-312]; learned emergency detector generalized on fresh blind sets where the lexical one failed [F-311] [F-441]; the independent reviewer agent changed 25 of 31 first-aid cards [F-313]. AI-reviewed, not clinically reviewed.
- Held-out movement across all of this: main 0.506 → cut 6 0.512 on v0.2, two seeds, +0.006: noise (group-B row 5).
- The fact table fires 0/110 on v0.2 and 0/58 on V-para, so cut 7's held-out numbers are cut 6's [F-359].

**Key decisions:** [D-032] (adopt cut 3), [D-034] (KVFIX → cut 4), [D-044] (CUT5-LITE), [D-045] (DETMAX → cut 6), [D-038] / [D-038] (freeze the claim build at cut 6, only answer-preserving fixes), [D-046] / [D-046] (cut 7 = cut 6 + FACTS r6, adopted on gates). **Reversal to show:** the 10-06 freeze ("v0.1 answers unchanged") was relaxed on 10-07 when cut 7 changed 8 v0.1 answers (group-A §2 item 4).

**Turning point:** 10-06: the audit counts 15 answer-identical arms and 0 ratio movement on the small model; "stop polishing the 4B".

#### 5 Systems: a frozen 4B build, a 35B deep tier, knowledge packs and a lite tier

The frozen claim build (cut 7) routes each question through a learned emergency detector and deterministic layers (calculator, unit and distance estimators, places, a 4,233-entity Wikidata table, first-aid cards and verbatim cited health excerpts); remaining questions are answered by Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 (Q4_K_M) from passages retrieved by SQLite FTS5 and 384-d bge-small lead vectors over offline packs (k = 6, 1,200-token context), after a keep step that removes off-topic and unsafe passages. The deep tier replaces the reader with Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (UD-Q2_K_XL; ≈ 3B active parameters per token; 400-token context; 200 answer tokens; thinking budget 512). Seven cuts were frozen between 2026-10-03 and 2026-10-07; cut 7 differs from cut 6 only by the fact table, which fires on 0/110 v0.2 and 0/58 V-para items, so cut 7's held-out numbers are cut 6's. Desktop runs execute the same TypeScript engine in Node with native components shimmed; desktop/phone parity is tested directly (§6.6). From 2026-10-20 the main 8 GB reader is Qwen3-1.7B (Q4_K_M) with refuse-by-default and a warning line (§6.8); the closed research engine ENGINE-RC (2026-10-23) adds the SEFIX-124 search fixes, a compact per-pack index (W78) and a shaped factbook (§6.10). The submitted system is a different implementation (§6.11).

*Facts: [F-375] [F-346] [F-585] [F-622]*

### 5 · The walls {#walls}

Span: 2026-10-03 → 10-06. Layers curious and tech: https://r4topunk.github.io/boar-research/research/walls.md.

**In one sentence.** Oracle tests showed where the small model's ceiling was: handing it the perfect passage helps, but getting that passage, and knowing what isn't in the kit, was the wall; bigger dense models, better prompts and better retrieval variants all failed.

**Key facts (v0.1 dev, Opus unless noted):**
- Oracle ladder: closed-book 0.487 · engine 0.507 · question-chosen passages 0.567 · gold passages 0.606 · Haiku no-web 0.653 (raw, 1 seed, n 57) [F-314].
- Retrieval v2 put the gold sentence in context 7 → 18/56 times yet lowered quality −0.021 [F-443].
- Perfect Wikipedia retrieval buys at most ≈ +0.005–0.017; most of the oracle gain came from web-only facts [F-992].
- Retrieval scorecard: recall@5 0.333; coverage is the largest failure bucket (49 %) [F-453].
- Model line closed for the 4B tier: Qwen3.5-4B 0.437, Gemma 4 E4B 0.495, Qwen3.5-9B 0.488, Ministral 8B 0.457 vs 0.487 [F-450].
- Longer-answer persona: Δ −0.044, confident-wrong 10 → 20 [E-027] [F-433]. A completeness instruction made the 35B longer but less correct (correctness 3.89 → 3.10) [F-579].
- 4B loss anatomy: gap to Haiku +0.121 net; biggest buckets have no live lever [F-317].
- DEEPREAD: the 35B reads gold passages about like the 4B (0.634 vs 0.606, +0.029, CI −0.004…+0.063): its advantage is knowledge [F-455] [F-578].

**Key decisions:** [D-010] (strategy memo: Android-only, three fronts, stop list), [D-012] (close the big-pack front, kill rule K1), [D-029] (park retrieval after rv2), [D-039] (stop answer-identical 4B arms; reopen the deep tier), [D-037] / [D-037] (v0.2 burnt → dev).

**Turning point:** 2026-10-06 14:06, the pipeline audit; same day v0.2 declared burnt because its plaintext sat in a private repo's git history.

#### The small model's walls (v0.1 dev)

Oracle runs on v0.1 (n = 57, 1 seed, Opus, raw) bracket the 4B: closed-book 0.487, engine 0.507, question-chosen passages 0.567, gold passages 0.606, Claude Haiku without web 0.653. The 35B reads the same gold passages only slightly better (0.634, +0.029, −0.004…+0.063), so its advantage is stored knowledge. A retrieval rewrite increased gold-sentence presence 7 → 18 of 56 yet lowered quality (−0.021); 25–35B MoEs form a closed-book plateau at ≈ 0.60 (0.596–0.613); 4–9B alternatives do not beat Qwen3-4B (0.437–0.495 vs 0.487).

*Facts: [F-314] [F-443] [F-034] [F-455] [F-450]*

#### 8 A registry of what did not work

We keep a public registry of 76 lever families (61 closed, 13 not detected, 2 measurements; a private registry continues to 98 rows) with, for each: what was tried, set and judge, effect with CI, minimum detectable effect where the test had one, and the condition that would reopen it. Families include larger closed-book models, prompt and persona changes, sampling presets, best-of-2 and self-verification, routing between tiers, re-ranking, query rewriting, corpus size, Wikipedia variants, computed verdicts, fine-tuning data, speculative decoding and quantization. Five closures based on n ≈ 20 slices with CI upper bounds ≥ +0.03 are relabelled here as "not detected at MDE 0.08" (R31, R83, R84, R85, R97), following an outside critique.

*Facts: [F-487] [F-932] [D-073]*

### 6 · The deep tier {#deep-tier}

Span: 2026-10-02, 10-06 → 10-10; dropped from delivery 10-21. Layers curious and tech: https://r4topunk.github.io/boar-research/research/deep-tier.md.

**In one sentence.** The one lever that beat noise was a much bigger model, a 35B mixture-of-experts with only about 3B active per token, and letting it think for 512 tokens before answering; it climbs the ladder from 0.26 to 0.44 floor-adjusted on the bounty-style set (desktop only, dev-style data), and still wins no head-to-head. It never ran on a phone: on 2026-10-21 the author decided that no 35B deep mode is delivered for the bounty; the deep tier stays in the record as a roadmap with its desktop numbers ([D-147] / [F-1532];; open fronts OF-1 and OF-2 dropped, `data/status.json`).

**Key facts (V-para unless noted; Opus; 2 seeds unless noted; deep-tier V-para numbers are dev-style):**
- First deep test on v0.1: +0.060 (+0.021…+0.101), 0.565 vs 0.505, n 57, 2 seeds, dev [F-033].
- Closed-book plateau of 25–35B MoEs ≈ 0.60 vs 4B 0.487 (v0.1, 1 seed) [F-034].
- Deep, no thinking: raw 0.467 (0.439–0.494), floor-adj 0.329 (0.294–0.362), 0/51 [F-005].
- Thinking 1024: floor-adj 0.422 (0.385–0.459); gain +0.093 (+0.050…+0.137) floor-adj, the largest single gain [F-007] [F-008].
- Budget curve (floor-adj): 0 → 0.329, 256 → 0.387, 512 → 0.436, 1024 → 0.422, 3072 no further gain (3072: 1 seed, Haiku) [F-593].
- 512 vs 1024: raw +0.011 (−0.010…+0.031), floor +0.014 (−0.012…+0.039) at 0.55× the time (p50 79 s vs 143 s, desktop) [F-010] [F-010].
- Recommended config H: raw 0.553 (0.524–0.581), floor-adj **0.436** (0.401–0.472), common-mode floor CI 0.387–0.486, 0/51; selected as best of ≥ 8 deep configs (winner's curse ≈ 0.01–0.02) [F-009] [F-009].
- Three seeds: raw mean 0.550 (SD 0.020); floor-adj mean 0.432 (SD 0.025) [F-012].
- On v0.2 (dev, 1 seed): raw 0.608 (0.575–0.641), floor-adj 0.508 (0.467–0.550), 0/1/109: CI straddles 0.50 [F-013].
- Remaining loss on V-para: 59 % absent knowledge, 40 % wrong facts [F-1184] [F-630].
- Closed with numbers: Gemma 26B + thinking (−0.028 raw, 27 % faster), thinking 4B (+0.026, CI crosses 0), best-of-2 selectors (chance), sampling presets, context 1200, top-100k Wikipedia pack on the deep tier (−0.034, crowding), 3-bit quant (+0.004, not detected) ([F-608], -34, -60, -59; [F-999]).
- Retrieval still matters for the deep tier: no-pack −0.045 (−0.083…−0.011) [F-1000].

**Key decisions:** [D-013] (run the deep tier, report it separately with its latency), [D-031] (park it, 10-04), [D-039] (reopen it, 10-06), [D-056] / [D-056] (thinking budget 512), [D-068] (keep retrieval on the deep path), [D-067] (deep line closed on desktop, 10-10), [D-058] (seed-noise rule; raised from 0.03 to 0.05 on 10-16), [D-147] (author, 2026-10-21: no 35B deep mode delivered; roadmap only, with desktop numbers).

**Turning point:** 2026-10-08 20:20, DEEPTHINK: thinking adds +0.093 floor-adjusted, the biggest step on the ladder.

#### 6.2 Model scale and test-time compute

All deep-tier rows were measured on V-para after it became development-style and on v0.2 after it was burnt; they are development evidence, desktop only. On V-para (Opus, two seeds): deep without thinking raw 0.467 (0.439–0.494), floor-adjusted 0.329 (0.294–0.362); with a 1024-token thinking budget 0.542 / 0.422 (0.385–0.459); with 512 tokens 0.553 (0.524–0.581) / 0.436 (0.401–0.472), common-mode floor-adjusted CI 0.387–0.486; with 256 tokens 0.514 / 0.387 (0.349–0.426). Every row wins 0 of 51 in each seed. Thinking (1024 vs none) adds +0.093 (+0.050…+0.137) floor-adjusted, the largest single effect we measured; 512 vs 1024 is parity (+0.014, −0.012…+0.039) at 0.55× the wall time; 256 vs 1024 loses −0.028 raw (−0.056…−0.003); a 3072 budget adds nothing (the model stops near 1.3k tokens; 1 seed, Haiku). The 512 configuration was selected as the best of at least eight deep configurations on V-para, so a winner's-curse discount of ≈ 0.01–0.02 applies; over three seeds its floor-adjusted mean is 0.432 (SD 0.025). On v0.2 the 512 configuration scores raw 0.608 (0.575–0.641), floor-adjusted 0.508 (0.467–0.550), W/T/L 0/1/109 with one seed; the 1024 configuration with two seeds scores 0.612 (0.581–0.644) / 0.514 (0.475–0.554).

*Facts: [F-005] [F-459] [F-006] [F-007] [F-008] [F-014] [F-605] [F-009] [F-012] [F-020] [F-464] [F-013] [F-460] [F-010] [F-011] [F-606] [F-593] [F-1231] [F-607] [F-750] [F-608] [F-465] [F-1170] [F-188] [F-004] [F-363]*

#### 6.3 Right but thin: dimension shares, reference length and the loss map

Decomposed by rubric dimension, the 512 configuration on V-para is above 0.50 floor-adjusted on correctness alone (0.660, 0.608–0.712) and well below it on completeness (0.301) and usefulness (0.341); the 4B is 0.427 on correctness. Re-judging the same answers against references condensed to ≤ 80 words moves the 512 configuration from 0.412 to 0.514 (0.456–0.578) floor-adjusted (seed 42, Opus), a paired +0.102 (+0.068…+0.144); half of that shift comes from the shortened references scoring lower themselves, and we attribute ≈ 17 % of the gap to reference length and ≈ 83 % to substance. This is not a bar reading: references were altered and n is one seed. A loss map attributes 59 % of the remaining V-para loss to knowledge absent from both the kit and the model and 40 % to wrong facts; numbers and dates dominate wrong-fact loss. All of English Wikipedia (Aug-2025 + a 2026-10-01 delta) verifiably holds the missing fact for 9 of 34 absent bounty-style items, a lower bound.

*Facts: [F-284] [F-466] [F-190] [F-467] [F-468] [F-1184] [F-630] [F-470] [F-1008]*

### 7 · A phone on a desk, and in a hand {#phone}

Span: 2026-10-02 → 10-22. Layers curious and tech: https://r4topunk.github.io/boar-research/research/phone.md.

**In one sentence.** The desktop stand-in was trustworthy for answer quality, and the frozen build matched it on real phones, but the phone exposed bugs and memory limits the desktop hid. The deep tier never ran on a phone (the author dropped it from delivery on 2026-10-21); the 8 GB phone runs of 10-20/21 changed the main engine (chapter 11).

**Key facts:**
- The 4B was killed by the OS on an 8 GB Android while loading: ARM weight repack copied ≈ 2.3 GiB into anonymous memory [F-686] [F-691].
- iPhone 13 run matched the desktop proxy (0.394 vs 0.395) [F-684].
- First real-phone run: our own KV-cache save-path bug re-prefilled the prompt every question (≈ 55–65 s), hidden by the desktop shim [F-710] [F-715].
- Cut 6 on an 8 GB Galaxy A15: 73/73; phone 0.561 (0.507–0.617) vs desktop 0.558/0.560; v0.1 dev, n 57, Opus judge.v1-med [F-024].
- Cut 7 on a 12 GB-class phone (POCO X6 Pro, 10.7 GiB usable, Android 16, airplane, no INTERNET permission): 72/72; raw 0.529 (0.481–0.575) = desktop 0.529, floor-adj 0.403 vs 0.402, paired −0.000 (−0.026…+0.028); v0.1 public dev, n 57, Haiku L1 judge; fast-tier p50 30.7 s, TTFT p50 18.5 s, decode 5.5 tok/s; PSS 5.88 GB peak during load, ≤ 4.23 GB after [F-023] [F-771] [F-772].
- The A15 and X6 ratios are not comparable in level (different judges) (group-A §4).
- Deep tier on a phone: never run (as of 2026-10-24; OF-1 dropped by the author's 2026-10-21 decision, [D-147]). Projection 1.9–2.8 min per answer at budget 512 on a Pixel 8 Pro CPU, from third-party public rates and our arithmetic [F-766]. Earlier (10-09) estimate was 3.5–5 min at budget 1024 (group-B row 6).
- Expert streaming fork on desktop CPU: 14–17 tok/s at ≈ 2.8 GiB RSS, judged-equivalent (0.625 vs 0.634, Δ −0.010, CI −0.042…+0.018, v0.1 dev, 1 seed, Opus). Desktop only; flash-bound projection ≈ 4 tok/s (UFS 3.1) / ≈ 6 tok/s (UFS 4.0) with compute [F-036] [F-036] [F-793]. Cross-built for Android arm64 on 2026-10-19; phone speed and memory never measured ([F-2118];; OF-2 dropped).
- 8 GB phone (Pixel 8a, bench app, 2026-10-20/21): the 4B at 29–46 s per answer and one low-memory kill; the 1.7B at 13–16 s; this is chapter 11 [F-1418].
- Long sessions: no quality drop out to turn 15 (turns 6–15 in-session/standalone 1.136, 0.993–1.320; reference = BOAR's own standalone answer, Haiku L1, 80 agent-written questions); latency grows to ≈ 22 s at turns 14–15 vs ≈ 8 s standalone [F-030] [F-895].

**Key decisions:** [D-024] (repack-aware memory fit, Android only), [D-034] (KVFIX), [D-035] (no-network APK by construction), [D-046] / [D-053] ("no device exists", 10-07; reversed in practice 10-14), [D-119] (expert streaming supersedes earlier loader ideas on paper).

**Turning point:** 2026-10-14 19:26, DEVICE-X6: the frozen build on a 12 GB-class phone gives the same judged quality as the desktop.

#### Device parity and speed

The frozen build (cut 7) on a 12 GB-class phone (MediaTek MT6897, 10.7 GiB usable, Android 16, airplane mode, no INTERNET permission) answered 72/72 items; on the 57 judged public v0.1 items, judged by Haiku L1, phone raw 0.529 (0.481–0.575) equals desktop 0.529, floor-adjusted 0.403 vs 0.402, paired −0.000 (−0.026…+0.028). Routing tier matched 60/60 and instant answers were byte-identical 16/16; model text was identical on 3/44 items (sampler differences). Earlier, cut 6 on an 8 GB phone scored 0.561 (0.507–0.617) vs desktop 0.558/0.560 under Opus judge.v1-med; the two phone studies are not comparable in level. Phone fast-tier p50 is 30.7 s (desktop 7.5 s on an M1 Pro; ×3.4); PSS peaks at 5.88 GB during load and stays ≤ 4.23 GB after. The deep tier never ran on a phone and was not delivered (author, 2026-10-21; [D-147]); two on-device engines are judged-equivalent to the desktop server on identical contexts (bmoe −0.012, −0.045…+0.020; expert streaming −0.010, −0.042…+0.018; v0.1, 1 seed, Opus), and a deep + 512 answer is projected at ≈ 1.9–2.8 min on a Pixel 8 Pro CPU from third-party rates.

*Facts: [F-037] [F-036] [F-793] [F-766] [F-023] [F-771] [F-772] [F-773] [F-024] [F-775] [F-776] [F-777] [F-778] [F-779] [F-780] [F-781]*

#### Multi-turn and lite tier

Over 10 five-turn sessions and a 15-turn extension (80 agent-written questions, Haiku L1, reference = the system's own standalone answer, not the frontier), in-session answers score 1.136 (0.993–1.320) of standalone on turns 6–15; latency rises to ≈ 22 s at turns 14–15 vs ≈ 8 s. A 1.7B lite reader with X2b equals the plain 4B only on pack-matched items (−0.007, −0.031…+0.018); on the claim kit 1.7B − 4B = −0.111, and at identical contexts the 1.7B reads worse (−0.070, −0.094…−0.044, n = 97). An earlier internal summary ("the lite gap is reach, not reading") was retracted on this evidence. §6.8 reports the 1.7B as main engine from 2026-10-20.

*Facts: [F-916] [F-030] [F-1081] [F-1082] [F-1279] [D-113]*

### 8 · The agent lab {#agent-lab}

Span: 2026-10-01 → 10-24. Layers curious and tech: https://r4topunk.github.io/boar-research/research/agent-lab.md.

**In one sentence.** One independent author ran this as a small research organisation made of AI agents: a coordinator that freezes rules and logs everything, researchers in lanes that propose but never measure, independent reviewers that decide wording, and an unattended loop; most ideas died for free, and the rules got stricter after every mistake.

**Key facts:**
- Lanes wrote technique cards: retrieval 19, models 22, evaluation/safety 23 [F-953].
- 101 closed arms: 54 closed at 0 judge calls, 10 at Haiku L1, 12 at L1 → Opus, 25 Opus directly [F-915] [F-873].
- Unattended loop 10-11 12:10 → 10-14 19:09: 133 ticks (28 idle); ≈ 12.0k Claude calls, of which ≈ 10.5k judge calls (Opus 4,851 + Haiku 5,660); mini 44.4 h + MacBook 18.1 h of generation; 1 dev lever; ≈ 31 avoidable machine-hours ([F-893] corrected-18, -22).
- 29 numbered rule changes in 12 days [F-899]; every pass/fail rule hashed before the run: 65/65 verified on 10-10, 16 of 17 re-verified by an outside critic on 10-16 ([F-1169] corrected).
- Incidents logged openly: a 10-hour run produced 45/120 empty answers without a smoke test [F-641]; the same 35B model file deleted twice by housekeeping ([F-756] corrected); judge authentication expired [F-228].
- Yield collapsed after the first week: 15 adopted improvements, all 10-04 → 10-08 [F-094]; 0 V-para floor-adjusted points per 1,804 judge calls in the 10-11/12 cycle ([F-1007] corrected).
- Second phase (10-18 → 10-24): the author delegated seven open decisions to the coordinator, which adopted the recommended options [D-123] [D-124]; about 200 frozen-criterion arms ran, mostly 0-LLM replays and Haiku screens (`data/experiments.json` [X-198]…); a two-stage screen (GATE v2) set its bar from measured "do-nothing" arms, which already "fix" 23–31 % of problem items by chance [F-2073] [D-141]; a pipeline audit found 33 issues, 6 P0 [F-1908]; an independent direction review on 10-19 said "stop opening arms" and was followed only partly [D-129]; one overnight run generated 2,855 answers and judged none, leaving the choice of judge runs to the author [F-1726] [D-176].

**Key decisions:** [D-008] (lanes), [D-009] (freeze every criterion), [D-027] (no human review: independent reviewer agent + "AI-reviewed, not clinically reviewed"), [D-063] (fail-closed judge), [D-061] (Power block), [D-069] (unattended loop), [D-073] (relabel under-powered negatives), [D-094] (Rule 29 experiment economics), [D-095] (LOOP v2).

**Turning point:** 2026-10-10 13:30, the R&D process review (10 agents, 76 findings): "measurement machine better than typical, pointed at the wrong target"; deliverables unbuilt [F-846].

#### 4 Discipline: frozen criteria, exposure ledger, fail-closed judging, and a judge funnel

Each experiment ("arm") compares one change with a named control under a criterion written before the deciding run and frozen by sha256; verdicts may add dated addenda but not edit the criterion. 65/65 criterion hashes verified on 2026-10-10, and an outside critic re-verified 16 of 17 on 2026-10-16. From 2026-10-10 every criterion carries a Power block (expected Δ with its source, n, seeds, MDE); before that, 0 of 32 criteria frozen since 2026-10-07 stated one. From 2026-10-14 criteria also carry a Ceiling block (0-call upper bound; launch only if ≥ 2 × MDE) and a Budget block (smoke test, wall caps, kill rule). Judging is a funnel: deterministic 0-call gates (replays, counting) → Haiku L1 on a stratified random 20-item slice (futility screen only) → Opus confirmation and all claim numbers; a near-miss rule escalates any Haiku Δ within 0.01 of a threshold to Opus. Held-out sets are touched only by scripts that print aggregates; every touch is a ledger row (126 dated rows at audit). Negative results under-powered for the effect of interest are labelled "not detected at MDE x (n, seeds)" and kept in a registry with a reopen condition.

**Second phase (2026-10-18 → 10-24).** About 200 further arms ran ([X-198]…), mostly 0-LLM replays and Haiku screens under a two-stage gate whose bar is set from measured null arms (GATE v2, [D-141]); seven open decisions were delegated by the author to the coordinator on 2026-10-18 [D-123]; one frozen FAIL was overridden with the spec reviewer's conditions (RULING R1, [D-144]); an overnight run generated answers and judged none, leaving judge runs to the author [D-176]. Who decided is labelled on every decision row.

**Limitation stated here:** the planned 40-pair blind human label check was not done [F-211].

*Facts: [D-009] [F-1169] [D-061] [D-094] [D-057] [D-064] [D-073] [F-843] [F-185] [F-231]*

### 9 · Knowledge packs {#packs}

Span: 2026-10-12 → 10-14. Layers curious and tech: https://r4topunk.github.io/boar-research/research/packs.md.

**In one sentence.** When the bar stopped moving, the author pivoted to a product question: small, openly licensed offline libraries the user picks; one matching pack helps a little, many packs crowd each other out, and the real headroom is getting the one fact-bearing chunk into the prompt.

**Key facts (180 pack self-test items, agent-written from pack text, dev; not a bar lever):**
- 11 packs published with cards, licences and 20 public self-test questions each (Stack Exchange Q&A, first aid, MedlinePlus, a world factbook, Simple English Wikipedia; licences PD / CC0 / CC BY / CC BY-SA only) ([F-1028], -66; [D-080]). Count: 7 at 00:01 and 9 at 02:30 on 10-13, 11 by 19:34 (group-A §2 item 8).
- One matching pack: +0.042 (+0.024…+0.062) Opus; +0.032 (+0.016…+0.050) Haiku [F-025].
- All packs as peers: fact article kept 68 → 46/180, quality −0.019 (−0.035…−0.003) Opus [F-026].
- Top-1 pack routing fails: 0.25 (vote) / 0.58–0.61 (4B zero-shot) vs a 0.85 bar [F-1026].
- Oracle: inject the known fact chunk: +0.095 (+0.070…+0.122) [F-027].
- X2b (append the retrieved article's neighbour chunks + budgeted dense candidates): fact present 35 → 102/180; +0.066 (+0.043…+0.091) Opus; inert on the bounty-shaped claim kit ([F-028], -89; [F-1076]).
- The deep tier gains nothing from any pack: −0.002 (−0.020…+0.016) [F-029].
- V-para is not pack-matched: wave-1 packs cover 1/34 absent bounty-style items [F-091].
- All of English Wikipedia verifiably holds the missing fact for 9 of 34 absent bounty-style items: a lower bound, "at most about a quarter" ([F-1008]; group-B row 3).

**Key decisions:** [D-078] (pivot to packs; conditional in-pack quality), [D-079] (pack-authoring workflow), [D-080] (format 2, licence policy, never NC), [D-084] (publish packs that pass the four-artefact check), [D-086] (oracle cell first), [D-087] (routing closed; rule + quota optional), [D-092] (X2b recommendation), [D-083] (default-eligible vs user-selected). **Reversal to show:** "facts are not in Wikipedia" (10-12 morning) withdrawn the same afternoon [D-076].

**Turning point:** 2026-10-13 23:11, ORACLE-ST: the ceiling is reach, not reading; it led directly to the only lever of the pack line.

**Continued in chapters 11, 13 and 14:** with the 1.7B as main engine the pack line was re-measured on real development questions (no pack gain there, [F-2080]), re-framed as delivery (chapter 13) and became the author's closing thesis in a conditional form (chapter 14). The 4B-era numbers above stay as measured; they describe the 4B, not the 1.7B.

#### Knowledge packs (pack-matched development items)

On 180 pack-matched self-test items (agent-written from pack text; development data; one seed; deterministic 4B generation) one matching pack improves the 4B by +0.042 (+0.024…+0.062) under Opus and +0.032 (+0.016…+0.050) under Haiku. Installing nine packs as peers reduces fact-article survival from 68 to 46 of 180 and costs −0.019 (−0.035…−0.003). Top-1 routers reach 0.25–0.61 accuracy against a 0.85 bar. Injecting the known fact chunk yields +0.095 (+0.070…+0.122); HEADPASS-X2b raises fact-chunk presence from 35 to 102 of 180 and yields +0.066 (+0.043…+0.091) (Haiku +0.056), with +0.177 (+0.098…+0.263) on the 30 items where the chunk became newly present; on the bounty-shaped claim kit it is inert. The 35B gains nothing from packs (−0.002, −0.020…+0.016). These are conditional, in-pack results and are not evidence about the bar; questions written from the same text the retriever indexes favour retrieval.

*Facts: [F-025] [F-1025] [F-029] [F-026] [F-1026] [F-027] [F-1027] [F-222] [F-028] [F-1063] [F-1064] [F-095] [F-1076]*

### 10 · Measuring the measurer {#measurer}

Span: 2026-10-02 → 10-21. Layers curious and tech: https://r4topunk.github.io/boar-research/research/measurer.md.

**In one sentence.** Claude wrote the questions, wrote the references and judged them, so the project measured its own instrument: judge noise is tiny, seed noise is not, and a judge from another company scores everything about 0.10 higher while keeping the same ranking and a near-zero win-rate.

**Key facts:**
- Second Claude judge (Fable 5.1): same winner 453/456 [F-1142].
- Haiku 5.5-low vs Opus on v0.1: r 0.922, κ 0.651, ratio −0.069 (lead with these; "same winner 54/57" is near-uninformative because the reference wins ≈ 100 % of items) ([F-996] OVERCLAIM note).
- Local open-weights judge (Gemma 4 26B): +0.11 lenient, κ 0.32/0.55, same ranking ([F-164], -47).
- Opus test-retest: σ ≈ 0.003 raw; per-item r 0.96; winner 51/51 [F-019].
- Seed noise: SD 0.020 raw / 0.025 floor on the deep tier; two seeds differ −0.039 (−0.072…−0.011) ([F-012], -34).
- Reference length: shortening references to ≤ 80 words moves H floor-adj 0.412 → 0.514 (s42); ≈ 17 % of the gap is length, ≈ 83 % substance [F-467].
- Correctness alone: H floor-adj 0.660 (0.608–0.712) on V-para; completeness 0.301, usefulness 0.341 [F-284].
- Cross-family judge (post-hoc, 408 + 660 calls, same rubric, orders and blinding): V-para 4B raw 0.497 / floor 0.361; H raw 0.667 / floor 0.577 (0.519–0.632); win-rate 0.00–0.01. v0.2: 4B 0.617 / 0.517 (2 seeds); H 0.714 / 0.639 (1 seed); deep − 4B gap +0.097 vs Claude +0.096; win-rate 2.7 % / 6.4 % vs 0 % [F-017] [F-017] [F-017] [F-018] [F-018] [F-490] [F-1208] [F-232].
- Outside critique: numbers real (15/17 re-derive), internal summaries overstated; 7 re-wordings applied [F-227] [D-113].
- Later calibration (10-20/21, dev): Haiku and Opus agree on confident errors (κ 0.75) far better than on "correct" (κ 0.49; 0.22 on warned answers); Opus finds 98 correct answers Haiku misses vs 10 the other way, so Haiku-only correctness rates are low-biased [F-2083] [F-1432]. judge.v1 gives a bare refusal U 0.058 (0.037–0.081), not zero [F-2081]: the reason the second ruler adds a stage-1 zero (chapter 12).

**Key decisions:** / (hold the cross-family pilot; done later with OpenAI gpt-5.6-sol via the Codex CLI), [D-049] (Haiku as L1), [D-050] (open judge for ranking only), [D-057] (near-miss rule), [D-072] (common-mode CI), [D-122] / [D-115] (lower judge is the headline; family named next to every ratio).

**Turning point:** 2026-10-16 19:01, the cross-family judge: the deep tier crosses 0.50 floor-adjusted only under the other family, and the win-rate does not move.

#### 7.1 One family wrote, referenced and judged: what changes under another
