Items (v0.2, V-para), references and the judge all come from the Claude family. We ran four checks. A second Claude judge (Fable 5.1) agrees with Opus on 453/456 verdicts. Haiku 5.5-low tracks Opus on v0.1 with r = 0.922, κ = 0.651 and a −0.069 level offset (agreement on the winner, 54/57, is near-uninformative because the reference wins almost every item) and compresses paired gaps to 0.70–0.95× of Opus's on pack arms and as low as 0.25× on one 4B-vs-deep pair. A local Gemma 4 26B judge is +0.11 lenient (κ 0.32/0.55) but preserves the deep − 4B ranking (+0.026 vs +0.029). Post hoc, the author re-judged existing traces with an OpenAI model using the same rubric, orders and blinding (408 calls on V-para, 660 on v0.2). It scores every configuration higher: on V-para the 4B rises from 0.413 / 0.261 to 0.497 / 0.361 and the 512 configuration from 0.553 / 0.436 to 0.667 / 0.577 (0.519–0.632); on v0.2 the 4B rises to 0.617 / 0.517 (two seeds) and the deep configuration to 0.714 / 0.639 (0.579–0.695) (one seed). The deep − 4B gap is preserved (V-para +0.171 vs +0.139; v0.2 +0.097 vs +0.096), per-item Spearman is 0.88–0.97, and win-rate stays near zero (V-para 0.00–0.01; v0.2 2.7 % and 6.4 % vs 0 %). Per the analysis plan, when two families differ by more than 0.05 raw the lower is the headline; we report the Claude numbers as headline and the cross-family numbers beside them.

**Caveat line under the figure:** "Cross-family runs were not pre-registered; their reports live with the held-out data and were not opened by the authors of this page; CIs for the 4B floor-adjusted cells were not available."

*Facts: [F-1142] [F-996] [F-1153] [F-1187] [F-164] [F-583] [F-017] [F-018] [F-490] [F-1208] [F-232]*

#### Noise budget

Re-judging unchanged answers with Opus gives σ_judge ≈ 0.003 raw (per-item r = 0.96; winner 51/51). Re-generating answers is the dominant noise: on the deep tier, seeds 42/43/44 give raw 0.533 / 0.572 / 0.544 (SD 0.020; floor-adjusted SD 0.025), and two seeds of the same configuration differ by −0.039 (−0.072…−0.011), a CI excluding zero. The 4B on V-para is seed-stable (identical ratios across seeds; per-item r = 0.81), and the desktop 4B path is byte-deterministic on a fixed host (20/20). A single 20-item Haiku pass carries ±0.03–0.04 of judge noise, about the size of the decision threshold, so slices screen for futility only; "hardest-20" slices inflated deltas 3–10× and were retired. The house reading rule is that a one-seed deep-tier Δ on V-para below 0.05 is seed noise (raised from 0.03 on 2026-10-16).

*Facts: [F-019] [F-012] [F-020] [F-618] [F-463] [F-476] [F-1166] [F-184] [F-199] [F-1195] [D-058]*

#### Multiplicity and selection

Across ≈ 60 judged comparisons, ≈ 1.5 false "CI low > 0" results are expected at α = 0.05; the large levers survive a Bonferroni-style correction (X2b z ≈ 5.5, LITE5 z ≈ 6, thinking z ≈ 4.2). The larger risk is selection on the same development sets (winner's curse on the deep configuration; levers designed on the 180 self-tests), which is why development and held-out readings are separated throughout.

*Facts: [F-1079] [F-1078]*

#### Two judges on labels, refusals and correctness (2026-10-20/21)

On double-labelled development units Haiku and Opus agree on confident errors (κ 0.75) far better than on "correct" (κ 0.49; 0.22 on warned answers); Opus finds 98 correct answers that Haiku misses vs 10 the other way, a +0.02 U shift [F-2083]. A Haiku confident-error count moves by about ± 1.3 per 100 on retest of identical answers. judge.v1 gives non-answers a positive score (bare refusal 0.058, hedge 0.053, fluent no-content 0.016; [F-2081]), and attempts to fix this inside the rubric flipped 5–7 of 40 confident-error verdicts [F-1955], hence the stage-1 zero of §3.6. Reference draws matter little: two uncapped Opus draws move U by ≤ 0.015 [F-2114]. Same-family judge lift in the literature is 3.4–8.4 points for open-model families and untested for Claude and GPT [F-2115].

### 11 · A smaller engine for 8 GB phones {#small-engine}

Span: 2026-10-18 → 10-21. Layers curious and tech: https://r4topunk.github.io/boar-research/research/small-engine.md.

**In one sentence.** On a real 8 GB phone the 4B was too slow and once killed by the operating system, so on 2026-10-20 the author made Qwen3-1.7B the main 8 GB engine, for latency and memory and explicitly not for quality. Two days of screens found no small model, prompt, decoder or gate that closes the 1.7B's reading gap at the same phone time, and the product rule became "refuse by default when no source is kept, with a warning line on what is shown".

**Key facts (dev data throughout; bench app or desktop research engine, never the submitted app):**
- Why no 8 GB lever could move the bounty-style number: on V-para the 4B's gap of 0.586 ratio points splits into wrong-from-memory 0.309 (23 items), absent knowledge 0.239 (24), thin 0.038 (4), refusals 0 (Opus judge.v1, seed 42, single-seed labels ± 0.05; [F-1406]). The fact is in the installed kit for 6 of 51 items and in any pack on disk for 10 of 51 [F-1407]. Estimated ceiling of all 8 GB levers on V-para: about +0.01–0.02 raw [F-1411].
- Honest prompt for the app's longer style: honesty clauses cut the audited wrong-claim rate 0.231 → 0.062 (paired −0.169, CI −0.281…−0.073; Claude Opus sentence audit, 15 agent-written chat turns per arm, 407 claims, dev) at no judged-ratio cost [F-1394] [F-1397].
- The pivot: on a Pixel 8a (8 GB) the 4B decoded 3.6–6 tok/s, answered in 29–46 s and was killed once at 4.4 GB RSS; the 1.7B decoded 13–16 tok/s and answered in 13–16 s (9 public dev questions, before batched lookups; [F-1418]). The author made the 1.7B the main 8 GB engine and the 4B an optional "more complete" tier ([D-134] / [F-1386]).
- Batched pack lookups (937 → 48 SQL calls per retrieval, retrieval byte-identical 390/390) cut the 1.7B's time to first token on the phone from 9.12 to 5.55 s (n 9; [F-1422], [F-1423]).
- 73-question phone runs (bench app, Pixel 8a, v0.1 dev, one run each): 1.7B p50 4.2 s over all items, PSS 3.39 GB; Gemma 4 E2B 11.8 s, PSS 4.52 GB; 4B 26.0 s complete (older engine), PSS peak 4.76–4.92 GB [F-1565] [F-2078]. **Caveat that travels with the 4.2 s:** it covers deterministic answers and declines (the 1.7B declined 35 % of v0.1); its model-path p50 is about 12 s; never set it beside the 13–16 s of the 9-question runs.
- The cost is reading. Under Opus (judge.v1 floor-adjusted ratio "U", v0.1 51 dev, one seed per rung): 4B − 1.7B +0.109 (+0.063…+0.160); 4B − Gemma E2B +0.098 (+0.054…+0.146); 1.7B − closed-book 1.5B +0.090 (+0.009…+0.170), which under Haiku is +0.038 (−0.023…+0.098), so that last step is judge-dependent [F-2077]. At identical pack contexts (54 pack self-tests, Haiku raw): 4B 0.650, LFM2.5-8B-A1B 0.554, 1.7B 0.529 [F-1401].
- Screens that did not close it (GATE v2, two-stage; [F-2072], [F-2117]): six prompt, decoding and confidence levers (fixes 1–4 of 21–23 confident errors, bar 6; token-probability AUC 0.530); decoder-level grounding [D-159]; Ministral-3-3B with a citation prompt passed stage 2 (Opus +0.047) but at about 3× phone time and below the 4B (−0.037 Opus), closed as dominated [D-189] [F-1933]. Gemma 4 E2B: Haiku +0.028, a FAIL by 0.002; Opus +0.031 (+0.005…+0.058), a GO by 0.001 [F-2076]; on the phone 11.8 s vs 4.2 s and +1.1 GB; kept as an opt-in proposal only [D-143].
- Honesty surface: the author set "no source → refuse by default, with a 'show anyway' control" [D-138] [D-149]. A groundedness gate cut visible confident errors 7 → 3 of 177 under an Opus re-judge (Haiku 10 → 4), false refusals 0 of 14, at about +9.3 s per answer projected for the Pixel 8a (5.1 s measured on a desktop); it is not in any app [F-1430] [F-2074]. Revealed answers behind "show anyway" were 11 correct to 16 confident errors in an Opus census [F-2084], so the button is a liability: it sits behind a second confirmation and never on health [F-1633]. The warning line's precision is 0.39–0.40 and recall 0.65–0.67 on the 1.7B (Haiku / Opus; [F-2085]). No drift detected over five turns [F-1957]. AI-reviewed, not clinically reviewed.

**Key decisions:** [D-123] / [D-124] (delegated decisions D1–D7: no v0.3, site only as v1.0 at closure), [D-129] (direction review: consolidate), [D-134] (1.7B main engine), [D-141] (GATE v2), [D-149] (refuse by default), [D-159] (decoder grounding closed), [D-186] (keep Q4_K_M), [D-187] (1.7B on latency and memory, not quality; model screens parked), [D-189] (Ministral closed). **Reversals to show:** the 10-20 morning proposal "answer under a warning line" was replaced the same evening by refuse-by-default ([D-135] → [D-149]); the 10-19 release of a safety-failing patch was reversed the same day [D-128].

**Turning point:** 2026-10-20 ~11:50, the author: "Qwen3-1.7B becomes the main engine".

#### 6.8 Latency and memory over quality: the 1.7B as main engine

A V-para diagnosis decomposed the 4B's 0.586 ratio-point gap into wrong-from-memory 0.309 (23 items), absent knowledge 0.239 (24), thin 0.038 (4) and refusals 0 (Opus, seed 42, labels ± 0.05), with the fact present in the installed kit for 6 of 51 items; the estimated ceiling of all 8 GB levers on V-para was ≈ +0.01–0.02 raw [F-1406] [F-1407] [F-1411]. On a Pixel 8a the 4B answered in 29–46 s and was killed once at 4.4 GB RSS, the 1.7B in 13–16 s (9 public dev questions; [F-1418]); the author made the 1.7B the main 8 GB engine on 2026-10-20 [D-134]. Under Opus on CV5 51 (judge.v1 floor-adjusted ratio of sums, one seed per rung) the 4B leads the 1.7B by +0.109 (+0.063…+0.160) and Gemma 4 E2B by +0.098 (+0.054…+0.146); the 1.7B's lead over a closed-book 1.5B is +0.090 (+0.009…+0.170) under Opus and +0.038 (−0.023…+0.098) under Haiku, i.e. judge-dependent [F-2077]. Two-stage screens (GATE v2; the bar = the largest measured null-arm net + 2, after null arms "fixed" 23–31 % of problem items; [F-2073]) closed prompts, decoding, token-confidence gates (AUC 0.530), decoder grounding, fine-tuned readers and small-model swaps; Gemma 4 E2B's stage-2 verdict flips with the judge (Haiku −0.002 below the bar, Opus +0.001 above; [F-2076]) at 2.8× phone time. A groundedness gate cut visible confident errors 7 → 3 of 177 under an Opus re-judge (Haiku 10 → 4), false refusals 0/14, at ≈ +9.3 s per answer projected on the phone [F-1430]. The reveal-anyway control returned 11 correct to 16 confident errors in an Opus census [F-2084]. No drift was detected over five turns [F-1957].

### 12 · A second ruler (bench v0.4) {#new-ruler}

Span: 2026-10-19 → 10-24. Layers curious and tech: https://r4topunk.github.io/boar-research/research/new-ruler.md.

**In one sentence.** The first ruler scored a desktop engine against Claude-written references with a Claude judge on Claude-written questions. For the submitted app the project wrote a second one: 75 new questions frozen on 2026-10-20 before any system answered them, written half by each judge family, scored as U-total with a zero for non-answers, two judge families and a split by whether the packs hold the answer. As of 2026-10-25 it has references from both families, a desktop-twin run of the submitted app's pre-rename engine that the author published as history (0 of 71 wins; lower family below the 0.50 bar), and an on-phone run in progress that will carry the headline.

**Key facts:**
- Design (10-19): a public ruler with a true-zero utility, uncapped two-family web references, items written outside the judge family where possible, and the submitted app as the scored system ([D-131] / [F-1383]).
- Bench v0.4: 75 items (71 headline + 4 anchors taken from the example questions in Vitalik Buterin's post that inspired the bounty, scored outside the headline), frozen 2026-10-20 16:45, sha f9ad2f2f, before any system answered [F-2070] [F-1353]. Candidate writers: Claude 36, OpenAI gpt-5.6-sol 34 [F-1416]. 329 checklist points supported on the open web (at least one family, none contradicting; the 32 balance-round points by both). It is **not** written outside the Claude family: half is Claude-written, a stated deviation [G-ruler-v04]. Its item text, references and drafts were not public until the record closed [D-195] and were published on 2026-10-27 in boar-bench (`bench/v0.4/`).
- Metric: U-total, a ratio of sums of (rubric mean − 1) for the app over the reference, so the rubric floor maps to 0; health items weigh 0.5 with weight-1 printed beside ([D-137]; the weighting was decided after the items existed, [F-1389]); verdict = the lower of the two families, "meets the bar" only if CI low > 0.50 with all gates passed [G-u-total].
- Why a stage-1 zero: judge.v1 gives a bare refusal U 0.058 (0.037–0.081), a hedge 0.053, a fluent no-content answer 0.016 (Haiku, 30 v0.1 dev ids; [F-2081]). A binary-checklist judge v2 failed its retest gate (CE retest 0.966 vs a needed 0.974; [F-1431]). RULING R1 kept judge.v1 unchanged and added DECLINE2STAGE, a classifier that zeroes detected non-answers; it was a coordinator override of a frozen FAIL, accepted with conditions by the spec reviewer ([D-144] / [F-1529]).
- Spec r3 (sha 0fac2286, 20:48) and r4 (sha 82772e33, 21:18) were frozen on 2026-10-21 before any app answered a v0.4 item [F-2109]. Verdict arm A∪: the app with all six persona packs installed at once [D-139] [D-156].
- References: Claude half 75/75 frozen before any app answer (uncapped, median 703 words, median 6 sources) [F-2110]; OpenAI gpt-5.6-sol half 75/75 on 2026-10-24 20:05, 0 hard failures [F-2212].
- Information available (counts only; label lists quarantined): the A∪ packs hold the answer for 19 of 71 headline items, partly for 25, not at all for 27 (strict 15 / 23 / 33) [F-2111]. 7 current-city items carry 10.7 % of headline weight and no app could answer them [F-2113] [F-1960].
- Exposure: on 2026-10-24 two engines answered v0.4 for the first time (desktop twins, Claude half only, stage 1 not run). Those numbers stay internal (one of the two engines is the native engine branch, whose numbers stay with the app maintainer; AD-15 (b)) and are dev/parity evidence, never a verdict; any later engine change counts as developed after exposure [F-2108].
- The scored system is the submitted APK on a phone [D-151] [D-191]. The phone run on v0.4 is DEVICE-FINAL (landed 2026-10-25, chapter 16); as of 2026-10-24 20:34 none existed.
- Final run (RULER-FINAL, 2026-10-24 20:34): BoarLite's final engine b4ef94f3 on its desktop twin, 71 headline items, one seed (the spec asks for two; the author's choice), each judge family against its own references, stage 1 not run [F-2214] [D-204]. The ruler is now exposed to three engines. Published by the author's decision of 2026-10-25 as history: 0 of 71 wins under both families (one gpt-5.6-sol tie); U-total (desktop twin of engine b4ef94f3) Claude Opus 0.164 (0.123–0.208), OpenAI gpt-5.6-sol 0.245 (0.194–0.300); the lower family, 0.164 (0.123–0.206), is below the 0.50 bar [F-2215] [X-405]. Information-available split, Claude family: 0.164 where the installed packs hold the answer (n 19), 0.174 partly (n 25), 0.155 not at all (n 27): with the information present, the 1.7B did not deliver it [F-2217]. The paired delta against the native engine branch stays internal, because it prints that branch's number (U44). They are numbers for b4ef94f3: the shipped app, LabRat 7788924a, adds the Rat persona line to the grounding prompt after this run [F-2225]. The on-phone re-run of v0.4 on LabRat (DEVICE-FINAL, three seeds under Claude Opus, seed 42 under gpt-5.6-sol) started on 2026-10-25 under a criterion frozen before generation ([F-2227]; OF-8); no result is in this record.

**Key decisions:** [D-131], [D-132], [D-133] (freeze; one item dropped after both families contradicted it), [D-137], [D-138], [D-139], [D-144] (RULING R1), [D-151], [D-156], [D-157], [D-158], [D-195]. **Supersessions to show:** the v0.3 path to an unexposed number (D5, 2026-10-18, [F-1374]) → v0.4, which is exposed and half Claude-written; "the ruler was frozen on 10-20" → the *item set* was frozen on 10-20, the first frozen spec is r3 on 10-21 [F-1628].

**Turning point:** 2026-10-20 16:45: the v0.4 item set is frozen before any system has seen it.

#### 3.6 A second instrument for the submitted app

Because the first instrument scored a desktop engine against Claude-written references on Claude-written items, a second ruler was specified for the submitted app [D-131]. Bench v0.4 has 75 items (71 headline; 4 anchors taken from the example questions in Vitalik Buterin's post that inspired the bounty, outside the headline), drafted by Claude (36 candidates) and OpenAI gpt-5.6-sol (34), cross-fact-checked (329 checklist points supported on the open web by at least one family with none contradicting), and frozen on 2026-10-20 before any system answered (sha f9ad2f2f) [F-2070] [F-1416]. The headline statistic U-total is a ratio of sums of rubric mass above the floor (mean − 1) against uncapped frontier-plus-web references from both families, with health items at weight 0.5 (weight-1 beside; decided after the items existed, [F-1389]) and a stage-1 classifier that zeroes detected non-answers (DECLINE2STAGE), because judge.v1 scores a bare refusal at U 0.058 (0.037–0.081) [F-2081]. A binary-checklist judge v2 failed its pre-set retest gate [F-1431]; keeping judge.v1 with the stage-1 zero (RULING R1) overrode a frozen FAIL and was accepted with conditions by the spec reviewer [D-144]. Spec r3 (sha 0fac2286) and r4 (sha 82772e33, adding an information-available split, FACT-AVAIL, and ORACLE / ORACLE-0 rows) were frozen on 2026-10-21 before any app answer [F-2109]. The verdict arm installs all six persona packs (A∪); the verdict is the lower family per bootstrap draw with CI low > 0.50 and all gates. FACT-AVAIL labels: AVAILABLE 19 / PARTIAL 25 / NONE 27 of 71 (strict 15 / 23 / 33), lists quarantined [F-2111]. As of 2026-10-24 20:34: references 75/75 for both families (Claude median 703 words; gpt-5.6-sol completed 20:05, 0 hard failures, [F-2212]); the set counts as exposed from 2026-10-24 [F-2108] and has now been answered by three engines on desktop twins. The final run (RULER-FINAL, [F-2214], [D-204]) scored BoarLite's engine b4ef94f3 with one seed (spec: two), each judge family against its own references (not the two-family mean), stage 1 not run, no errata; the spec labels desktop-twin numbers dev/parity evidence. Published by the author on 2026-10-25 as history: win-rate 0 of 71 under both families (one gpt-5.6-sol tie); U-total (desktop twin of engine b4ef94f3) 0.164 (0.123–0.208) Claude Opus, 0.245 (0.194–0.300) gpt-5.6-sol; minimum over families 0.164 (0.123–0.206), below the bar by the pre-registered rule; FACT-AVAIL (Claude) AVAILABLE 0.164 (n 19), PARTIAL 0.174 (n 25), NONE 0.155 (n 27), so the information's presence did not raise U-total [F-2215] [F-2217]. The paired delta against the native engine branch is withheld (it carries that branch's absolute; the app maintainer's numbers stay internal). The engine it measured, b4ef94f3, precedes the rename to LabRat: 7788924a changes the grounding prompt's identity line ("You are Rat…"), so the RULER-FINAL number is not attributed to LabRat without that caveat [F-2225] (the ruler run predates the Rat persona line). DEVICE-FINAL (criterion frozen 2026-10-25 03:3x, [F-2227]) re-runs v0.4 on the phone with LabRat 7788924a, three seeds under Claude Opus and seed 42 under gpt-5.6-sol, with a phone-vs-desktop parity read against b4ef94f3 that is not a verdict; running, no results in this record.

### 13 · Delivery, not coverage {#delivery}

Span: 2026-10-19 → 10-23. Layers curious and tech: https://r4topunk.github.io/boar-research/research/delivery.md.

**In one sentence.** With the 1.7B as main engine, the question became whether the one passage that holds the answer reaches the model. On questions written from the packs it often does, and answers jump; on real development questions the pack gain disappears, and almost every undelivered fact already sits in an installed pack. Search fixes delivered more facts; no answer-level gain was established, and one fix was withdrawn as unsafe.

**Key facts (all dev; "U" = judge.v1 floor-adjusted ratio; Haiku unless named):**
- Self-tests vs real items: on 60 topical pack self-tests the pack gain sits on items where the pack adds the key fact, +0.139 (+0.075…+0.201), n 27; the same cell on real development items is −0.010 (−0.077…+0.050), n 10 [F-2080]. The self-test gain is not a word-overlap artefact (reweighted to real overlap +0.064, +0.035…+0.095; [F-1965]).
- Question form decides retrieval (48 pack facts × 9 phrasings, agent-written, 0-LLM replay): the gold chunk is kept for 50 % of base questions, 83 % of yes/no, 25 % of situational, 10 % of entity-free, 8 % of bare follow-ups [F-2092]. When the reference chunk is kept, the 1.7B scores U 0.876 (n 43, 2 confident errors) vs 0.185 (n 147, 75 confident errors), a between-item comparison on pack-written items [F-2093].
- The author, 10-22: "packs are the strategy"; small focused packs, full Wikipedia as a negative control [D-161] [D-162].
- A stricter count: from 10-22 a fact is "delivered" only when it sits inside one kept chunk; article-level counting had overstated delivery by 8–13 facts [D-165] [F-2095].
- Search fixes on MAIN 92 keyed items, chunk level: none 21 → global-IDF merge 28 → SEFIX-124 42 → SEFIX-ALL 47 [F-2095]. SEFIX-ALL's fourth fix (F3, a health no-source fallback) fired on 21 of 65 safety probes and unsafe answers rose 9 → 13 (blinded agent reading, one seed; AI-reviewed, not clinically reviewed); it was withdrawn [D-164] [F-2097]. The safe set SEFIX-124 gives +0.013 (−0.008…+0.035) on all 97 (two seeds): not a lever, adopted for delivery only [F-2025].
- Between items, delivery does not separate answers: delivered 0.420 vs not 0.419 (+0.001, −0.071…+0.069); within the same items, +0.044 (+0.009…+0.082, n 42, two seeds), and an Opus check on 28 delivered general questions +0.013, inside noise [F-2098].
- Where the undelivered facts are: 44 of 50 already sit in the default 13-pack kit (K13); new packs reach at most about one fact each [F-2100], so no new packs were built [D-173].
- Reading cost: a compact index inside each pack (W78) cut the data read per question from 125.09 to 21.26 MB and the cold first stage from 620 to 92 ms, with 42/42 facts kept (desktop replay; phone unmeasured) [F-2103].

**Key decisions:** [D-127], [D-160], [D-161], [D-162], [D-164], [D-165], [D-172], [D-173], [D-193], [D-194]. **Corrections to show:** F1b's "45 delivered" is 32 at chunk level; SEFIX-ALL's "55" is 47 [F-2095]; the Opus +0.173 "where the fact arrives" (n 22, selected slice) came from the run that included the withdrawn F3 [F-1593] [F-2096].

**Turning point:** 2026-10-22, the author's "packs are the strategy", followed the same day by the chunk-level rule that made the target measurable.

#### 6.9 Self-test gains do not transfer; delivery does not separate answers

On 60 topical pack self-tests the pack gain concentrates on items where the pack adds the key fact (+0.139, +0.075…+0.201, n 27); on real development items the same cell is −0.010 (−0.077…+0.050, n 10), and the self-test gain is not a lexical-overlap artefact (+0.064 after reweighting to the real overlap distribution) [F-2080] [F-1965]. Retrieval depends on question form (hit@kept 83 % yes/no, 50 % base, 25 % situational, 10 % entity-free, 8 % bare follow-ups; [F-2092]). From 2026-10-22 delivery is counted at chunk level (article-level counts overstated it by 8–13; [D-165]). On MAIN 92 keyed items, delivered facts rose 21 → 28 (global-IDF merge) → 42 (SEFIX-124) → 47 (with F3, withdrawn after unsafe answers rose 9 → 13 on 65 probes) [F-2095] [F-2097]; the safe set changes U by +0.013 (−0.008…+0.035; Haiku, two seeds) [F-2025]. Between items, delivered vs not scores 0.420 vs 0.419 (+0.001, −0.071…+0.069); within items +0.044 (+0.009…+0.082, n 42, Haiku), Opus on 28 delivered general items +0.013 [F-2098]. 44 of 50 undelivered facts already sit in the installed kit [F-2100].

### 14 · Closing the research: what a small model needs {#closure}

Span: 2026-10-23 → 10-24. Layers curious and tech: https://r4topunk.github.io/boar-research/research/closure.md.

**In one sentence.** On 2026-10-23 the author closed the research lines; on 2026-10-25 he stated the thesis the record presents: **small models need external knowledge, and the project, having learned that, built a harness around a small model's real capabilities, tuned for the app user's experience** (a health gate, QuickMath, pack search and delivery, the Succinct persona, a fixed check-the-source line, refusal behaviour) [F-2236] [D-215]. The closing tests are its evidence and its honest limits: with the matching pack the 1.7B is right on 48 % of pack-written self-tests vs 26 % without, and on 65 % when the item's own article reaches the model vs 28 % otherwise; but the article arrives only 54 % of the time, no pack reached the 0.75 bar fixed in advance, and the gain did not transfer to real development items. The sentence the author first wrote on 2026-10-23, "right whenever the content is in a pack", is kept as the hypothesis those tests checked: they support it only in that conditional form. The afternoon turned to content (reshaping packs), the night to validating one closed engine, and the next day's judge kept the shortest answer style.

**Key facts (outcome-label shares unless named; Claude Haiku 5.5-low labels; Qwen3-1.7B, Succinct; seed 42; desktop twin, no phone; dev):**
- Closure: the author closed the research lines; the rest is acceptance tests on the app's desktop twin [F-1653] [D-167] [D-169].
- Thesis, first form (2026-10-23 12:19): "right whenever the content is in a knowledge pack, and the app built to answer well under that premise" ([D-170] / [F-1690]); the closing tests support it only in the conditional form [G-conditional-thesis]. Superseded as the thesis statement on 2026-10-25 ([D-215] / [F-2236]): small models need external knowledge; a harness built around a small model's real capabilities, tuned for the app user. Its limits include the real-item split: the self-test fact-added cell +0.139 (+0.075…+0.201, n 27) vs real development items −0.010 (−0.077…+0.050, n 10) (Haiku judge.v1 U, one seed; [F-2080]), and the app's desktop-twin ruler reading (lower family 0.164, below the bar; [F-2215]).
- PACKPROOF (180 pack-written self-tests of 9 packs): correct-any 0.48 with the pack vs 0.26 without, +0.23 (+0.16…+0.31) [F-1704]; 0.65 when the item's own article is kept (n 98) vs 0.28 [F-1705]; the own article is kept for 54 % and cited for 28 % (article-level; [F-1706]); 0 of 9 packs reach 0.75 (best 0.60, worst 0.25; [F-1707]). Without the pack: wrong and confident 0.17, wrong under the warning line 0.45, honest "unknown" 0.12 [F-1708].
- UXMATRIX (60 dev items): Succinct beats Detailed with and without the pack (correct-any ON 0.35 vs about 0.27; [F-1709], [F-1710]); with the pack off the model never says "I don't know" itself: every honest "unknown" is an engine decline, and the warning line shows on 75 % of answers [F-1711].
- Pack and search levers closed the same day (0-LLM replays): undelivered facts are a search problem, 44 of 50 already in K13 [F-2100]; dropping the Wikipedia packs loses MAIN facts 42 → 33, so they stay [F-1714] [D-172]; an oracle question rewrite would deliver only +9 facts (bar +10) [F-1715]; warning cited-but-unsupported answers would catch 9 of 26 wrong at a cost of 5 of 37 correct, NO [F-1712].
- CONTENT-FIRST (author, 15:3x): no model change; make the right chunk reach the 1.7B [D-174]. Shaped factbook (short sentences that name the country, no new facts): fact chunk kept 7 → 15 of 20; correct 5 → 10 of 20 (two seeds, Haiku); Opus judge.v1 U 0.316 → 0.436 (+0.121, +0.030…+0.221, two seeds); NOT-CONFIRMED by its frozen rule because of one new warned confident error [F-2104]. The 0.436 here is a factbook self-test U and has nothing to do with the deep tier's 0.436 on V-para.
- ENGINE-RC (night, one closed tree): every 0-LLM suite passed (identity 97/97 and 180/180; routes 103/110; the one letter-FAIL pre-existed); data read per question 125.09 → 21.26 MB; a false "Not found in this phone's offline library" line on 37 of 97 answers with kept passages fell to 0; 2,855 answers generated, 0 judge calls overnight [F-2105] [F-1722] [F-1725] [F-1726].
- Validation judge (2026-10-24, the page's numbers): Succinct correct-any 0.43 with the pack (right with source shown 0.30, wrong-unwarned 0.12), 0.22 without (wrong-unwarned 0.10); longer styles (one 4–5-sentence paragraph, two paragraphs) were right as often (0.42) but doubled wrong-unwarned answers (0.23, 0.25) [F-1727] [F-1728] [F-2106]. Follow-ups: carrying the subject brings the turn-1 source back (0.083 → 0.708) without changing accuracy (0.458 both) [F-1729] [F-2107]. The 10-23 → 10-24 Succinct shift (0.35 → 0.43) has no isolated cause in the record (engine changed in between; n 60, one seed).

**Key decisions:** [D-215] (thesis restated, 2026-10-25), [D-167], [D-168] (adopted for delivery: SEFIX-124, W78, Succinct for models ≤ 2 GB, Deep Research hidden), [D-169], [D-170], [D-171], [D-172], [D-173], [D-174], [D-175] (shaped factbook stays user-selected, unpublished), [D-176], [D-177] (wider append budget and best retrieval config stay out: dose/number probes changed), [D-179], [D-180].

**Turning point:** 2026-10-23 11:53, the author closes the research lines; at 12:19 a first thesis is stated, and by 14:2x the tests have reduced it to its conditional form; on 2026-10-25 the author restates the thesis as what was learned and built, with those numbers as its evidence and limits.

#### 6.10 Small models need external knowledge: what the closing tests support

The author closed the research lines on 2026-10-23 with the hypothesis "right whenever the content is in a pack" [D-167] [D-170]; on 2026-10-25 he stated the thesis as a design statement: small models need external knowledge, and the project built a harness around a small model's real capabilities, tuned for the app user's experience [F-2236] [D-215]. The numbers below are its evidence and its limits; they do not establish a quality level (U41–U43). Closing tests ran on the desktop twin with outcome labels (Claude Haiku 5.5-low; §2.13 of the claims page): on 180 pack-written self-tests of 9 packs (1.7B Succinct, seed 42), correct-any is 0.48 with the pack vs 0.26 without (+0.23, +0.16…+0.31); 0.65 when the item's own article is kept (n 98) vs 0.28; the own article is kept on 54 % and cited on 28 % (article level); 0 of 9 packs reach the 0.75 bar fixed in advance ([F-1704]…[F-1708]). The hypothesis therefore holds only in the conditional form, and on real development items the pack gain does not transfer (fact-added cell −0.010, −0.077…+0.050, n 10, vs +0.139 on self-tests; [F-2080]). Pack shaping (factbook) doubled delivery and correct answers on 20 self-tests and moved Opus U 0.316 → 0.436 (+0.121, +0.030…+0.221), NOT-CONFIRMED by one new warned confident error [F-2104]. The closed engine passed every 0-LLM validation suite and cut data read per question 125.09 → 21.26 MB [F-2105] [F-1722]. The 2026-10-24 validation judge kept Succinct: correct-any 0.43 vs 0.42 for longer styles, wrong-unwarned 0.12 vs 0.23–0.25 (UXMATRIX 60, seed 42) [F-1727] [F-1728]; the Succinct reading moved from 0.35 on 10-23 to 0.43 on 10-24 on the same items after engine changes, with no isolated cause. Subject carry restored the turn-1 source on follow-ups (0.083 → 0.708) without changing accuracy (0.458) [F-1729].

### 15 · One simple app: LabRat {#submission}

Span: 2026-10-15 → 10-25. Layers curious and tech: https://r4topunk.github.io/boar-research/research/submission.md.

**In one sentence.** Which app is submitted changed twice: the app maintainer's native app (decided 10-15, reaffirmed 10-21), then on 2026-10-24 BoarLite, a closed, offline, Succinct-only chat app of the author's own, renamed LabRat on 2026-10-25 ("LabRat (formerly BoarLite)"; below, BoarLite for events before the rename). In one evening (2026-10-24 17:39 → 20:34) BoarLite went from a decision to a final candidate (b4ef94f3): a health gate that shows fixed safe text when no health source is kept, one fixed line under every answer, factbook v1, conversions computed in code, and the bench search ported in a mode that skips health questions. It runs offline on a Pixel 8a. The search port was merged although its frozen criterion failed by the letter, because the author had accepted that health trade-off in advance; the record says so. Its ruler scores exist on the desktop twin of b4ef94f3 and are public as history (0 of 71 wins; lower-family U-total 0.164, below the 0.50 bar). That night the author cut the app down further (long-chat summary, PIN lock, Portuguese, the Expo/React Native tree), and on 2026-10-25 it became LabRat, whose assistant, Rat, is named by a new line in the grounding prompt: an engine change after the ruler run, so the ruler number belongs to b4ef94f3 and the final on-phone matrix (DEVICE-FINAL, completed 2026-10-25) measures LabRat 7788924a (the ruler run predates the Rat persona line).

**Key facts:**
- Answer style, research engine (dev): Succinct beats the longer styles on small models. On v0.1 51 (Haiku, desktop): 1.7B Succinct U 0.263 vs Detailed 0.224, Deep Research multipass 0.174 (2.6–5.6× slower) [F-1998] [F-2042]; on the app's 27 suggested topics, unsupported sentences Detailed 0.468 vs Succinct 0.283 (Haiku sentence audit; [F-2102]).
- 2026-10-24 14:25, the author: a closed, simple chat app built for one way of use: Succinct fixed; Deep Research, Detailed and the length setting removed; free follow-ups ([D-181] / [F-1701]).
- As of 2026-10-28, 2026-10-24 16:51, the author: BoarLite is the new bounty submission: no INTERNET permission, the full K13 kit in one APK (≈ 3.0 GB), Qwen3-1.7B fixed, English only ([D-183] / [F-1703], [F-1864]). Two of those choices were changed at 18:03 (next bullet); [F-1703] and [F-1864] carry `superseded_by`.
- 18:03, the author ([D-196] / [F-2189]): port a minimal health path; replace the ported warning line (D4) with one fixed line, "May contain errors; check the source.", under every answer [G-fixed-line]; keep factbook v1 (the shaped v2 is not in the app; D3 reverted); port the bench search before the submission under a frozen criterion.
- **Health gate** ([G-health-gate-bfu]; all counts 0 LLM, on the 65 dev safety probes; AI-reviewed, not clinically reviewed): the app's own lexical health test fixed only 8 of 65 probes vs 41 on ENGINE-RC, missing drug, dose and vital-sign wording [F-2191]. The B+FU detector (11 lexical rules + short follow-ups of a health turn; fitted on these probes, so in-sample) catches all 4 answers that had invented a dose figure with 0 new false fires on 251 non-health dev items [F-2192] [D-197]. After retrieval, 41–42 of 65 probes get the fixed text [F-2193] [F-2194].
- **The Wikipedia-health limitation:** the gate counts only the first-aid, MedlinePlus and health Q&A packs as health sources, so 12 of 60 health self-tests whose article sits only in a Wikipedia pack get the fixed text instead of an answer [F-2193]. The decision, delegated by the author at 19:32: ship with it, keep Wikipedia (dropping it cost facts 42 → 33), and add a curated list of medical Wikipedia titles after the submission, re-gated with the grounded-dose rule ([D-202] / [F-2206]).
- QuickMath computes pure conversions and arithmetic with no model, search or sources, never on health turns; the model preloads right after unpack; a 5-card onboarding replaces downloads, model choice and style [F-2200] [F-2199] [D-199].
- **The search-port trade-off** (SEARCHPORT; 0-LLM replays unless named; dev): ported to the native engine, the bench search fixes deliver more (MAIN keyed facts 26 → 40 at chunk level, own fact chunk 38 → 62–64 of 180, context ×1.07) [F-2195] [F-2196] [F-2207]. Safety: P1 failed its frozen gate (3 new dose-figure answers; [D-198]); the author then replaced kept-list proxies with the grounded-dose rule (a dose figure must appear in a shown passage; [G-grounded-dose-rule]; [D-200]), under which the port still failed (ungrounded figures 9 vs 5; [F-2203]). A third variant, ON_NO_HEALTH (search port off on turns the health predicate fires on; [G-on-no-health]), changes no probe's final path but still adds ungrounded figures, 6 vs 4: **its frozen verdict is not WORTH-IT (S1 failed by the letter)**; its usefulness screen (S2, UXMATRIX, Haiku labels, seed 42) passed its frozen bar: on the 51 items whose kept list changed, correct-with-source 9 → 15, correct-any 20 → 21, wrong-unwarned 31 → 30 [F-2207] [F-2208]. It was merged because the author had set a standing condition before the run: "I accept the health loss if it is worth it for the rest" ([D-203] / [F-2209]). The record shows both the failed criterion and the author's acceptance.
- **Final candidate** b4ef94f3 (19:40): 41 fixed / 1 exposure / 23 model answers on the 65 probes, identical with the port off, so the port changes no health path; release APK 3,044,169,517 B with no INTERNET permission [F-2210] [F-2211]. Two later UI-only commits (brand colours, an animated six-card tour; 10 files, 0 engine files) mean the APK is being rebuilt from 6aa7508a; the ruler run on b4ef94f3 stays valid [F-2213] [D-205].
- **On a phone** (Pixel 8a, airplane mode; one device, hand checks): first launch unpacks 3 GB in 14 s, 0 bytes over the network, 0 crashes, PSS 3.09 GB after 5 answers (APK 9d7fdc2e; [F-2198]); on the candidate APK the model is ready 18 s after launch and the first answer takes 11.9 s at 14.9 tok/s [F-2201]. The 6aa7508a release APK then passed its own offline smoke (0 B network, 0 crashes, PSS 3.23 GB; [F-2219], later superseded by the LabRat APKs).
- **Scored on the desktop, published as history:** the final ruler run on BoarLite's engine (desktop twin, one seed, both judge families; [F-2214]) won 0 of 71 and scored a lower-family U-total (desktop twin of engine b4ef94f3) of 0.164 (0.123–0.206), below the 0.50 bar ([F-2215]; chapter 12). By the author's decisions of 2026-10-25 the on-phone run of LabRat (DEVICE-FINAL) carries the headline, and this run is history with the code-difference note (AD-05, AD-23). A finding from that run: the chat shows the streamed text, so the pipeline's citation-support cleaning is not applied on the plain path [F-2218]. The author left it as a documented known limitation (Citations.applyShown, not fixed), so the measured engine stays the one judges install ([F-2232]; [F-2237]; AD-24).
- **Less app, on purpose (2026-10-24 21:30 → 10-25 01:11; owner decisions).** After the author's screens review (UI only; [F-2220]): the long-chat summary removed because on the Pixel the 1.7B used only the last 3 exchanges ([D-206] / [F-2221]); no PIN lock [D-207]; Portuguese removed, English only [D-208]; the Expo/React Native tree and code unreachable in the closed app removed (Detailed, adaptive routing, persona and length options, Deep Research beyond the recap; [D-209]); Settings simplified, 50 chats kept instead of 10, MIT licence texts in About [D-210]. 274 engine unit tests pass [F-2222].
- **LabRat (2026-10-25 02:20).** At the app maintainer's request the app became LabRat and its assistant Rat; package id, packs and the "Based on BOAR (MIT)" credit unchanged; smoke 6/6 against the baseline ([D-211] / [F-2224]). Logo n8, a magnifier whose ring is a rat's head, followed at 11:24 ([D-213] / [F-2226]; APK smoke [F-2235]).
- **The engine is not the ruler's engine any more, by one line.** The grounding prompt's identity line changed from "You are BOAR, an offline AI research app…" to "You are Rat, the assistant in LabRat…"; the engine module also lost code described as unreachable (124 files changed, almost all removals), checked by unit tests and a baseline smoke, not by a ruler rerun [F-2225] [F-2223]. **The RULER-FINAL number is for b4ef94f3; it is never attributed to LabRat 7788924a without the persona-line caveat** ( S37, U37).
- **DEVICE-FINAL (landed 2026-10-25).** At the author's request a final benchmark matrix ran on the Pixel 8a with the app itself answering, under a criterion frozen before generation: M1 v0.4 on three seeds (Claude Opus; gpt-5.6-sol on seed 42), M2 the 65 probes, M3 140 on-K13 self-tests, M4 UXMATRIX, M5 speed, memory and offline; claim numbers = M1 + M5 ([D-212] / [F-2227], [F-2228]). An APK install interrupted it at 11:28 and it was restarted [F-2229]. It landed on 2026-10-25 (OF-8): 0 of 71 wins under both judge families, below the 0.50 bar [F-2238]; report, criterion, aggregates and tools in boar-research rnd/research/coordinator/arms/device-final/, raw traces and judgments at the same path in boar-traces.
- **Hosting and install path.** The 3.04 GB APK is hosted on Hugging Face (author's OK 2026-10-25; GitHub release assets must be under 2 GiB) with an install page ([D-214] / [F-2230] / [F-2246]). Android developer verification may add an "advanced flow" (warning and a one-day wait) to browser installs of unregistered apps; the GrapheneOS test phone cannot show the judges' path, so a test on a certified phone is still to be done [F-2231].

#### 6.11 From the maintainer's app to BoarLite, renamed LabRat

**A pre-registered criterion failed by the letter and overridden.** The search port delivers more facts (MAIN keyed 26 → 40, chunk level, 0-LLM replay) but failed every frozen safety check: P1 gate d (3 new dose figures), then the grounded-dose re-gate (ungrounded figures 9 vs 5), then ON_NO_HEALTH's S1 (6 vs 4; no probe changes final path), while ON_NO_HEALTH passed its usefulness screen S2 (on the 51 changed UXMATRIX items, correct-with-source 9 → 15, correct-any 20 → 21, wrong-unwarned 31 → 30; Haiku labels, seed 42; [F-2208]). It was merged because the author had stated before the run that he would accept a health loss if the rest gained [F-2207] [F-2209] [D-203]. We report this as an adoption against a frozen verdict, not as a pass. The grounded-dose rule itself has a known hole: on the bench engine a shown passage's toxic threshold (150 mg/kg) was given as a dose and scored "grounded" [F-2205].

Known limits: health sources exclude Wikipedia, so 12 of 60 health self-tests with only a Wikipedia article get the fixed text (shipped, [D-202]); the chat path does not apply the pipeline's citation-support cleaning [F-2218], a known limitation the author chose not to fix before the measurement so that the measured engine is the installed one ([F-2232]; AD-24). The final ruler run on b4ef94f3 (desktop twin, one seed, both families; [F-2214], [F-2215]) is reported in §3.6 as history. No measurement in §6.1–§6.10 is a measurement of BoarLite.

**After the ruler run (2026-10-24 21:30 → 2026-10-25 11:24).** UI review, then a cleanup round of owner decisions: the Expo/React Native tree, Detailed, adaptive routing, persona and length options, Deep Research beyond the recap, the long-chat summary (on the phone the 1.7B used only the last 3 exchanges), the PIN lock and Portuguese removed; Settings simplified; licence texts in About ([D-206]…[D-210]; [F-2220]…[F-2222]). On 2026-10-25 the app was renamed **LabRat** at the app maintainer's request, its assistant **Rat** (7788924a, same package id; [D-211]). This is an engine change after the ruler: the grounding prompt's identity line now reads "You are Rat, the assistant in LabRat…" (was "You are BOAR…"), and the engine module changed in 124 files, almost all removals of code described as unreachable, checked by 274 unit tests and a baseline-matching device smoke, not by a ruler rerun [F-2223] [F-2225]. RULER-FINAL therefore measures b4ef94f3; LabRat 7788924a is measured by DEVICE-FINAL on the phone (OF-8, landed 2026-10-25; interrupted once by an APK install at 11:28 and restarted, [F-2229]) (the ruler run predates the Rat persona line). An open engine bug, Citations.applyShown not applied to the streamed answer, is left for the author: fixing it changes the engine and requires a ruler rerun [F-2232]. Hosting: Hugging Face (GitHub release assets < 2 GiB; APK 3.04 GB; [D-214]); Android developer verification may add an "advanced flow" for browser installs (scope unconfirmed; [F-2231]).

### 16 · Where it stands (live) {#honest-number}

Span: 2026-10-05 → 10-25. Layers curious and tech: https://r4topunk.github.io/boar-research/research/honest-number.md.

**In one sentence.** The research lines closed on 2026-10-23, and the submitted app (LabRat, formerly BoarLite) runs offline on a phone. Its headline number is the final ruler (bench v0.4) measured on the phone by DEVICE-FINAL, which landed on 2026-10-25 (author's decision of 2026-10-25, AD-05): 0 of 71 wins under both judge families, the lower family below the 0.50 bar [F-2238]. As of 2026-10-28, the record also holds history: the same ruler on the desktop twin of the pre-rename engine b4ef94f3 (one seed, before the Rat persona line) won 0 of 71 under both judge families with a lower-family U-total of 0.164, below the 0.50 bar; under the Claude judge the old ratio did not reach 0.50 on the earlier held-out sets; and no unexposed held-out number exists. The thesis the record presents is the author's: small models need external knowledge, and the app is a harness built around what a small model can really do [F-2236]; the outcome labels of the closing tests are its evidence and its limits. Three metric families stay separate. This chapter is finalized at closure (v1.0).

**Key facts, in three panels that never share an axis:**
- **Panel A, judge.v1 ratio (old scale; history since 2026-10-25, `history.old_scale`).** V-para (held-out at run time, Opus, 2 seeds): the frozen 4B build raw 0.413 (0.384–0.445), floor-adjusted 0.261 (0.224–0.300), 0 of 51 wins [F-001]. v0.2 (burnt → dev): raw 0.512 / floor-adjusted 0.388, 0/0/110 and 0/1/109 [F-002]. Bar reading: no configuration reaches floor-adjusted 0.50; the formal raw rule is met only by the desktop deep tier on development data [F-004]. Closest configuration (desktop, dev-style): floor-adjusted 0.436 (0.401–0.472), 0 of 51 [F-009]; never delivered [F-1532]. Cross-family (post-hoc): V-para 0.361 / 0.577 floor-adjusted, win 0.00–0.01 [F-017]; v0.2 [F-018]. Set status: both former held-out sets are now development data [F-038].
- **Panel B, outcome labels (closing tests; dev; pack-written where named; Haiku labels).** With the pack, correct-any 0.48 vs 0.26 without [F-1704]; 0 of 9 packs at 0.75 [F-1707]; 44 of 50 undelivered facts already in the kit [F-2100]; the shipped style on ENGINE-RC: correct-any 0.43, wrong-unwarned 0.12 [F-1727].
- **Panel C, the second ruler.** Bench v0.4 frozen [F-2070]; references of both families 75/75 [F-2110] [F-2212]. **On the phone (headline):** DEVICE-FINAL landed on 2026-10-25 (OF-8; criterion frozen before the run, [F-2227]): 0 of 71 wins under both families, the lower family below the 0.50 bar ([F-2238], [F-2239], [F-2240]; two seeds, 42 and 43). **On the desktop (history, `history.desktop_ruler`):** BoarLite b4ef94f3, one seed: 0 of 71 wins under both families; U-total Claude 0.164 (0.123–0.208), gpt-5.6-sol 0.245 (0.194–0.300); lower family 0.164 (0.123–0.206), below the 0.50 bar; information-available split as in chapter 12 [F-2215] [F-2217]; labelled "desktop twin, one seed, not a phone run" and "engine b4ef94f3, before the Rat persona line".
- **Product state.** Main engine Qwen3-1.7B [F-1386]; the 4B leads it by +0.109 under Opus on v0.1 51 dev [F-2077]; submission LabRat (formerly BoarLite; renamed 2026-10-25, [F-2224]), built from final candidate b4ef94f3 [F-2210] plus the Rat persona line and removed code [F-2225] [F-2223], offline on a Pixel 8a with the first answer in 11.9 s on a pre-rename APK [F-2201]; search port merged as ON_NO_HEALTH against its frozen verdict, by the author's prior condition [F-2207] [F-2209]; ships with the Wikipedia-health limitation [F-2206].
- Claim text: the prepared sentence is "BOAR is not shown to be half as good as frontier AI with web" (draft v4.2.4, [F-1245]). ### 17 · Open fronts and hand-off {#handoff}

Span: 2026-10-14 →. Layers curious and tech: https://r4topunk.github.io/boar-research/research/handoff.md.

**In one sentence.** As of 2026-10-28 two fronts are still open in the status file: the claim text (OF-5) and the shaped-pack publication (OF-7). The submitted app's delivery and scoring (OF-4, LabRat, formerly BoarLite: bundled build, Hugging Face upload and install page, its scores public by the author's decision of 2026-10-25) and the final on-phone matrix (OF-8, DEVICE-FINAL) landed on 2026-10-25; the ruler run (OF-6) landed on the desktop twin of b4ef94f3 and is published as history. Three earlier fronts were dropped, each by a dated decision: the deep tier on a phone (OF-1) and expert streaming on Android (OF-2) when the author ruled out a 35B mode (2026-10-21), and v0.3 (OF-3) when the delegated decisions chose no v0.3 before closure (2026-10-18). Each front lists what would change, in both directions; criteria are frozen in the research repository before each run. The deliverables already public stay usable by other teams.

**Key facts:**
- Public repos live 2026-10-15 10:07: boar-bench (139 files) and boar-research (411 files); on 2026-10-27/28 the open-source release added the retired held-out sets and the ruler v0.4 in boar-bench, the raw run traces (boar-traces) and the packs; scrubbed, mechanically gated, independently reviewed (41/44 findings applied) [F-1316] [D-105].
- Engine pull request to the upstream app opened 10-15 10:10 [F-1272]; later NUMGUARD r3 and HEALTHGAP r2 added (E-chron-late timeline).
- Pack uploads after 10-17: a fixed Simple English Wikipedia revision (a unit-conversion converter bug, 3,176 → 524 artefact chunks) on 10-21 and a knowledge-base index snapshot on 10-22 [F-1601] [F-1989]. The shaped factbook is drafted as user-selected only and unpublished (OF-7; [D-175]).
- A reusable 0-LLM retrieval bench (RETBENCH v1) is public in boar-research (rnd/research/coordinator/arms/retbench/, with its items, configs and tools) [F-1720].
- A hand-off package for the app maintainer is prepared; sending it waits for the author.
- [sentence withheld in this file; see https://r4topunk.github.io/boar-research/data/ or https://r4topunk.github.io/boar-research/research/<chapter>.md] Citations.applyShown stays a documented known limitation by the author's decision of 2026-10-25 ([F-2232]; AD-24).
- Power for any future bar test: at n = 110 a one-sided "> 0.50" needs a point estimate ≈ 0.53 (≈ 0.545 with one-seed run noise) [F-205]; v0.4's 71 headline items are fewer.
- Dropped: OF-1 (deep tier on a 12 GB-class phone, [D-147]), OF-2 (expert streaming on Android: built 10-19, never measured on a phone, [F-2118]), OF-3 (v0.3: no items; its role passed to v0.4, which is half Claude-written; [D-123] / [F-1374]).

**Key decisions:** closing-sprint decision 2026-10-14 21:59, [D-097], [D-100], [D-123] / [D-124] (delegated D1–D7; site only as v1.0 at closure), [D-147], [D-150] (article home: a project subdomain built from the public research repo; PLAN §1 PD-19), [D-175], [D-183].

**Turning point:** 2026-10-15 10:07: the record went public; 2026-10-24: the submission became the author's own app, so the remaining fronts are delivery and scoring, not research.

#### Limitations and open fronts

As of 2026-10-25 the record contains no unexposed held-out number and no number written entirely outside the Claude family: v0.3 was dropped (2026-10-18), and the second ruler is half Claude-written and was exposed on 2026-10-24. Its final run on BoarLite's engine (OF-6, landed 2026-10-24 20:34) is a desktop twin with one seed, published as history (lower family 0.164, below the bar); it measured b4ef94f3, before the Rat persona line of LabRat 7788924a; the on-phone run of LabRat (DEVICE-FINAL, OF-8) landed on 2026-10-25 as the headline (0 of 71 wins under both families, the lower family below the 0.50 bar; [F-2238]); with 71 headline items its power is below that of the 110-item design (at n = 110 a one-sided "> 0.50" needs a point estimate near 0.53; [F-205]). The deep tier never ran on a phone and was not delivered (OF-1 and OF-2 dropped, [D-147]). The thesis's evidence rests on pack-written self-tests labelled by one cheap judge with one seed. The human label check was not done. BoarLite's health rules are fitted on the 65 probes they are checked on, and its search port was adopted against a failed frozen safety verdict (§6.11). Open fronts (`data/status.json`, each with what would change in either direction; criteria frozen in the research repository before each run): OF-4 LabRat (formerly BoarLite) delivery (final bundled build, Hugging Face upload, install-path check); OF-5 the claim text (v4.2.4 prepared, posting not recorded, to be revised for LabRat and posted with a link to the article); OF-6 landed (published as history; b4ef94f3); OF-7 the shaped factbook (kept unpublished by the author); OF-8 DEVICE-FINAL, the on-phone matrix (landed 2026-10-25, the headline). Beyond closure: reading in small models, a pre-registered (not post-hoc) cross-family judge, and an item set written entirely outside both judge families.

*Facts: [F-205] [F-1252] [F-1297] [F-1253] [F-270] [F-211] [D-123] [D-147] [F-2108]*

#### Open fronts (status.json, as of 2026-10-28)

##### OF-1 · Deep tier on a 12 GB-class phone (dropped)

Question: Does the recommended deep configuration (35B mixture-of-experts + 512-token thinking budget) run on a 12 GB-class Android phone, at what latency and memory, and with the same judged quality as on the desktop?

Why it matters: Every deep-tier number in the record is desktop only; the phone time is a projection from third-party public rates, and the bounty is about a phone.

What would change, in either direction: If it runs with judged parity: the deep-tier rows in 'The deep tier' and 'A phone on a desk, and in a hand' gain a measured phone scope, the projection F-035 is replaced by a measurement, and 'Where it stands (live)' can describe the deep tier as a phone configuration. If it does not fit in memory, is too slow to use, or loses quality on the phone: the deep tier stays a desktop-only result, the phone standing remains the frozen 4B build (F-001, F-023), and the attempt is recorded as a negative result.

Note: Dropped by author decision on 2026-10-21: no 35B deep mode is delivered for the bounty; the deep tier appears only as a roadmap with its desktop numbers. No deep-tier phone run exists as of 2026-10-24; F-035 stays a projection.

Owner: author. Related: [F-009] [F-013] [F-023] [F-035] [F-037] [F-1532].

##### OF-2 · Expert-streaming engine on Android (dropped)

Question: Can the expert-streaming engine, judged equivalent to the desktop server on the 35B model, be built for Android and run within a phone's memory at a usable speed?

Why it matters: On a desktop CPU it runs the 35B model in under 3 GiB of RAM; on a phone only an analytic speed projection exists, and the Android build needs memory and thinking-budget work that is not done.

What would change, in either direction: If it builds and runs: OF-1 gains a low-memory path, and the analytic projection F-793 is replaced by a measured phone speed in 'A phone on a desk, and in a hand'. If it does not: the phone path for the deep tier rests on the other on-device engine (F-037), and the expert-streaming result stays a desktop-only finding (F-036).

Note: The expert-streaming engine was cross-built for Android arm64 on 2026-10-19; phone speed and memory were never measured. Dropped with OF-1 when the deep tier left the delivery (2026-10-21).

Owner: author. Related: [F-036] [F-037] [F-793] [F-2118].

##### OF-3 · Held-out set written outside the Claude family (bench v0.3) (dropped)

Question: What do the frozen build and the deep tier score on questions and references written outside the Claude model family and never exposed to the builders?

Why it matters: It is the only path to an unexposed held-out number: v0.2 is burnt and V-para is dev-style for everything after 2026-10-06. It also tests the judge-family self-preference threat at the item level, not only at the judge level.

What would change, in either direction: If items are written and scored before closure: their reading becomes the held-out number in 'Where it stands (live)' and in the claim text, in whichever direction it falls, under the analysis plan's lower-judge rule. If not: the record closes stating that no unexposed held-out number exists, and the current standing (F-001) stays the only held-out-at-run-time reading.

Note: No v0.3 was written (decision D5, 2026-10-18). Its role passed to the ruler set v0.4 (open front OF-6), which is not written outside the Claude family (half Claude, half OpenAI gpt-5.6-sol). The record therefore has no unexposed held-out number written outside the Claude family; F-001 remains the only held-out-at-run-time reading on the old scale.

Owner: author. Related: [F-001] [F-038] [F-205] [F-1251] [F-1282] [F-1374] [F-2070].

##### OF-4 · Scoring of the submitted app (LabRat, formerly BoarLite) (landed)

Question: How does the submitted app score on the frozen ruler, measured on a phone, and may its numbers be published?

Why it matters: The submission changed twice: the app maintainer's native app (2026-10-15, reaffirmed 2026-10-21), then BoarLite, the author's own closed app (2026-10-24). Research-engine numbers do not transfer to either app.

What would change, in either direction: The submitted app's numbers are public by the author's decision of 2026-10-25 (AD-15 (b)): the on-phone DEVICE-FINAL run of LabRat 7788924a (OF-8) becomes the headline in whichever direction it falls; the desktop-twin run of b4ef94f3 (one seed) stays as history with the persona-line caveat. Release-candidate scores of the app maintainer's app stay internal.

Note: As of 2026-10-24 20:34: BoarLite final candidate b4ef94f3 built (health gate, fixed line, factbook v1, QuickMath, search port ON_NO_HEALTH) and an earlier candidate smoke-tested offline on a Pixel 8a (model ready 18 s, first answer 11.9 s). Pending: the release APK rebuilt from 6aa7508a with two UI-only commits (0 engine files) and its phone smoke, APK hosting (above a 2 GB asset limit), a ruler run on the phone. Its ruler scores exist on the desktop twin and are internal-pending-author (PD-09 / AD-15); scores of the app maintainer's RC1 and of the native engine branch stay internal. Update 20:47: the final release APK (UI-only commits on top of b4ef94f3) passed its offline smoke on the Pixel 8a (F-2219); APK hosting remains. Update 2026-10-25: renamed LabRat at the app maintainer's request (7788924a, assistant Rat; same package id); the Rat persona line entered the grounding prompt after the ruler run on b4ef94f3, so that number is for b4ef94f3, not for LabRat 7788924a. Cleanup decisions: long-chat summary, PIN, Portuguese and the Expo/React Native tree removed, Settings simplified, licences in About. ### 18 · Reproduce it (appendix) {#reproduce}

Span: —. Layers curious and tech: https://r4topunk.github.io/boar-research/research/reproduce.md.

**In one sentence.** Everything that can be rerun is public, and what cannot be rerun is named.

**Key facts:** engine = public upstream commit `0cfd4a77` + arm patch; bench = boar-bench v0.1 (questions, references, judge, scorers); models and packs listed in BOM.md of boar-research; not reproducible: bit-identical judge outputs (closed model), the emergency-detector runner profile (not released); rerun steps: [How to reproduce the key results](https://github.com/r4topunk/boar-research#how-to-reproduce-the-key-results-step-by-step) in the boar-research README. Updated 2026-10-28: the retired held-out sets and the second ruler v0.4 (items, both reference halves, drafts) were published on 2026-10-27 in boar-bench (`bench/heldout/`, `bench/v0.4/`) with their runs in boar-traces, byte-identical to the hashes committed before opening except documented redactions; the [D-195] rule (no v0.4 text before the result card) ended with the record. Still private: personal correspondence, the app maintainer's data, usage and spend records, credentials, the private lab's working history (the public repos keep one commit per release; earlier releases remain in history). The 2026-10-18 → 10-25 arm reports are public in boar-research under rnd/research/coordinator/arms/, among them RETBENCH (retbench/), PACKPROOF (packproof/), UXMATRIX (uxmatrix/), X2B-BUDGET (x2b-budget/) and DEVICE-FINAL (device-final/). DEVICE-FINAL's M1 raw phone outputs, traces and judgments are in boar-traces (rnd/research/coordinator/arms/device-final/, listed with sha256 in TRACES.tsv); RETBENCH, PACKPROOF, UXMATRIX and X2B-BUDGET have their reports, frozen criteria and aggregates in boar-research, and their raw runs and judgments are not published (boar-traces holds only the PACKPROOF and UXMATRIX request files).

#### 10 What can be rerun, by whom, at what cost

The engine is a public upstream commit (0cfd4a77) plus per-arm patches; the benchmark (questions of every set, frozen references with provenance, judge, scorers, floor metrics), the raw run traces and the v0.3 plan are public; models and packs are listed with licences and revisions in the bill of materials. Every judgment row records judge model, CLI version, judge version and the sha256 of traces, questions and references, and everything after the judge is deterministic given the judgment rows. A full v0.1 judge pass is 114 calls (≈ 5 min at four shards). The retired held-out sets and the second ruler's items, references and drafts were published on 2026-10-27 (boar-bench bench/heldout/ and bench/v0.4/, runs in boar-traces; byte-identical to the hashes committed before opening, except documented redactions listed in bench/heldout/HASHES.md), so they can be rerun, but they are no longer unseen. Not reproducible from public material: bit-identical judge outputs (closed model; σ_judge ≈ 0.003) and the emergency-detector runner profile (base-model licence unknown; not released). Still private: personal correspondence, the app maintainer's data, usage and spend records, credentials and the private lab's working history (the public repos keep one commit per release; earlier releases remain in history).
